items.title: Município da Beira pede calma aos transportadores e marca reunião decisiva para a próxima semana

original_payload.original_title: Município da Beira pede calma aos transportadores e marca reunião decisiva para a próxima semana
original_payload.original_body:
Proposta de aumento da tarifa ainda não foi aprovada. Compensações prometidas pelo Governo Central há três meses continuam sem chegar e sem documento oficial.
Os transportadores semi-colectivos de passageiros da cidade da Beira ameaçam paralisar as suas actividades caso não seja aprovado o aumento da tarifa. Perante a ameaça, o Conselho Municipal da Beira pede calma e garante que a proposta já apresentada pela Associação dos Transportadores está a ser analisada.
A reunião que estava prevista para esta semana entre a edilidade e a Associação não se realizou. O encontro foi remarcado para segunda ou terça-feira da próxima semana, quando as duas partes vão debater, ponto por ponto, a proposta de aumento.
Segundo a Vereadora dos Transportes do Município da Beira, Flora Impula, a proposta ainda não foi aprovada pelo Executivo Municipal. Depois de passar pelo Executivo, o documento terá de seguir para a Assembleia Municipal, órgão que, por lei, tem competência para aprovar as tarifas.
“Entre segunda e terça-feira teremos um encontro no Município com a Associação para debatermos as tarifas propostas. Ainda não está aprovado pelo nosso Executivo. Depois da aprovação do Executivo, vamos fazer chegar o documento à Assembleia Municipal. Cabe à Assembleia aprovar, de acordo com o que está legislado”, explicou a Vereadora.
COMPENSAÇÕES QUE NÃO CHEGAM
Mais do que a tarifa, o que está a sufocar os transportadores são as compensações prometidas pelo Governo Central após a subida do preço dos combustíveis.
Já se passaram três meses desde o anúncio. Era suposto que a compensação começasse a ser paga no quarto mês, mas, até ao momento, nenhum transportador recebeu qualquer valor. O Município afirma que também não recebeu qualquer documento oficial a confirmar o fim ou a continuidade do programa.
“Nós recebemos uma informação de que o Estado ia dar compensações aos nossos transportadores, mas ainda não recebemos um documento indicando o contrário. Era bom que o Estado fizesse o mesmo que no passado, que mandasse um documento por escrito”, lamentou a Vereadora.
A governante sublinhou que a situação dos transportadores preocupa a edilidade, por ser o Município a entidade que lida directamente com os munícipes.
“A dor dos nossos transportadores é a dor dos municípios, porque quem vela pelos munícipes somos nós”, afirmou.
APELO CONTRA A GREVE
Enquanto aguarda por uma decisão formal, o Conselho Municipal apela aos transportadores para que não avancem com a greve nem pratiquem preços especulativos.
“Quero pedir aos nossos transportadores que tenham paciência, que esperem que os assuntos sejam aprovados de forma legal. Não façam preços especulativos. A greve não é bem-vinda. O que é bem-vindo é o munícipe ter transporte na hora que quer e para onde quer chegar”, apelou a Vereadora dos Transportes.
A reunião de segunda-feira é vista como decisiva para evitar a paralisação e encontrar uma solução que satisfaça os transportadores e os passageiros.

items.title: Nem sempre o tamanho interessa, há que haver trabalho

original_payload.original_title: Nem sempre o tamanho interessa, há que haver trabalho
original_payload.original_body:
Quem nunca ouviu esta advertência, vinda dos mais velhos e entendidos na matéria da vida: “Nem sempre o tamanho interessa” Pois é. Mas parece que o tamanho passou a interessar no Município da Cidade de Maputo.
Há alguns dias, o governo municipal teve a ideia de aumentar o tamanho das letras nas faixas que identificam as rotas dos transportes semi-colectivos de passageiros, numa tentativa de minorar o nível de encurtamento de rotas, que têm vindo a tomar proporções preocupantes e não só.
A edilidade decidiu aumentar o tamanho das letras para melhorar a visibilidade das rotas, facilitando a sua identificação tanto pelos passageiros como pelos agentes fiscalizadores. Mais do que isso, a medida pretende facilitar o reconhecimento dos infractores pelos agentes municipais que trabalham na via pública.
Neste sentido, o tamanho interessa? Sim. Mas o tamanho pode não ser de bom tamanho se não houver outro trabalho adicional.
Resolver parte dos problemas acima mencionados, cujo expoente máximo é o encurtamento das rotas, prática que acaba por criar um défice no bolso do pacato cidadão, não se consegue simplesmente aumentando o tamanho das faixas. É preciso adoptar outros mecanismos que obriguem os automobilistas a cumprir as regras e que permitam uma fiscalização efectiva.
Aumentar o tamanho das letras não vai diminuir as sessões de entrevistas matinais e ao fim do dia a que os passageiros são submetidos pelos famigerados cobradores. Muito menos vai reduzir a superlotação e os comportamentos nocivos que os passageiros do “chapa 100” são obrigados a suportar durante uma viagem de ida e volta para o trabalho, para a escola e para outros destinos.
O problema, portanto, não está apenas no tamanho das letras. Está na incapacidade de fiscalizar e fazer cumprir as regras e, sobretudo, na responsabilidade de quem devia garantir que o transporte público funcione em benefício de quem paga por ele.
Porque, convenhamos: pode-se aumentar o tamanho, mas, se não houver fiscalização à altura, o problema continuará exactamente do mesmo tamanho.
Na verdade, há tamanhos que deviam ser reduzidos, como o número de agentes colocados nos principais pontos da cidade, cuja actividade parece resumir-se à cobrança da receita do dia, em vez de fiscalizarem e fazerem cumprir as regras. A edilidade devia agir sem contemplações contra a má actuação e a corrupção dos seus próprios agentes, que, em muitos casos, ignoram deliberadamente as infracções cometidas na via pública. São esses os tamanhos que não precisam de ser acrescidos, mas, sim, reduzidos, se existe realmente vontade de resolver o problema.
O tamanho que precisa de aumentar é o número de autocarros de transporte público, em quantidade suficiente para responder à procura na região metropolitana e acabar, de uma vez por todas, com o drama diário dos citadinos.
Outro tamanho que precisa de aumentar é a extensão da rede rodoviária, sem esquecer a qualidade das estradas, cuja insuficiência e degradação contribuem para os congestionamentos e o caos na circulação no centro da cidade.
Afinal, não se resolve um problema de mobilidade aumentando apenas aquilo que é mais conveniente anunciar. É preciso atacar as verdadeiras causas, responsabilizar quem não cumpre as suas funções e investir naquilo de que os cidadãos realmente precisam.
Tamanho não é tudo , há que haver trabalho!

Novembro 9, 2026
O Tribunal Administrativo (TA) exerce a fiscalização das finanças públicas e emite o Relatório e Parecer sobre a Conta Geral do Estado (CGE), nos termos do artigo 229 da Constituição da República e da legislação aplicável, designadamente a Lei n.º 24/2013, de 1 de Novembro, alterada pela Lei n.º 7/2015, de 6 de Outubro, e a Lei n.º 14/2014, de 14 de Agosto, alterada pelas Leis n.º 8/2015, de 6 de Outubro, e n.º 13/2024, de 19 de Junho.
Em 29 de Setembro de 2026, o TA aprovou o Relatório e Parecer sobre a CGE de 2025 e remeteu-o à Assembleia da República. A apreciação deste documento constitui uma oportunidade para avaliar em que medida as irregularidades anteriormente identificadas foram corrigidas, que fragilidades persistem e que medidas foram adoptadas pelas entidades responsáveis em resposta às recomendações do Tribunal.

items.title: Ethiopia Pavilion Officially Opens at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye

original_payload.original_title: Ethiopia Pavilion Officially Opens at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye
original_payload.original_body:
Addis Ababa, November 9, 2026 (ENA)— The Ethiopia Pavilion officially opened today at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, showcasing the nation's climate leadership and green transformation to the global community.
The pavilion was inaugurated by Gedion Timothewos, Minister of Foreign Affairs and COP32 President-Designate, alongside Fitsum Assefa, Minister of Finance and COP32 Chief Negotiator.
The opening ceremony brought together diplomats, members of the Ethiopian delegation, representatives of international partner organizations, and global summit participants.
The pavilion serves as Ethiopia’s primary platform at COP31 to highlight its pioneering climate initiatives, including the massive Green Legacy Initiative, renewable energy expansion, and climate-resilient economic policy.
Furthermore, the dedicated space highlights Ethiopia’s readiness and strategic preparations as it gears up to host the upcoming COP32 summit, positioning the nation as a key continental voice in global climate diplomacy and sustainable development.

items.title: At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal

original_payload.original_title: At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
original_payload.original_body:
At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
Image source,  Getty Images
Image caption,    Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders estimates that 21 out of every 100 people who reach the Canary Islands by sea die during the crossing (file photo)
By  Ondiro Oganga
Published
9 November 2026, 08:16 GMT
Updated 54 minutes ago
At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports, citing an official source.
The interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established.
The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands.
Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors.
Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued.
President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings.
In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys.
"We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said.
The tragedy comes amid renewed concerns over the dangers facing migrant attempting to reach Europe by sea.
Walking Borders estimates that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the Canary Islands during the period it monitored.
Senegalese authorities said they had intercepted another boat, on Friday, carrying 142 migrants attempting to reach Spain.
Those on board included 23 women, two babies and two other children. Police said the group comprised nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria.
Meanwhile, a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro on Saturday following a surge in migrant arrivals.
More than 3,300 people have reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, according to local authorities.
This amounts to almost a third of the population on the island, one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants arriving from West Africa.
Fernando Clavijo, president of the Canary Islands regional government, described the situation as "absolutely unsustainable," reports the Reuters news agency.
The route has grown in prominence amid tighter controls and increased cooperation between European countries and North African states, which may have diverted some journeys away from the central Mediterranean.
Limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks are among the factors driving people to leave Senegal, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
For many young people, the prospect of finding work and earning more abroad remains a powerful incentive, despite the risks of crossing the Atlantic in overcrowded boat.
Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, according to the country's statistics agency.
The figure highlights the challenge facing President Faye's government as it seeks to create jobs for a predominantly young population that overwhelmingly voted for him in the 2024 elections.
In a statement on Sunday, Senegal's interior ministry said it would continue efforts to combat people-smuggling networks, including by strengthening cooperation with neighbouring countries.

original_payload.original_body:
Après 62 jours de captivité de dix habitants du village d’Oumba, dans le département de Madarounfa, les populations locales interpellent les autorités nationales afin d’obtenir leur libération. Elles réclament également la restitution d’une rançon de 3,5 millions de FCFA saisie lors d’un contrôle des Forces de défense et de sécurité.
Un raid nocturne ciblé au cœur du département de Madarounfa
Le 7 septembre 2026, aux alentours de 23 heures, une bande armée a fait irruption dans la localité rurale d’Oumba, située dans la commune de Sarkin Yamma. L’incursion s’est soldée par l’enlèvement de dix habitants. Le profil des victimes souligne la vulnérabilité des cibles choisies par les assaillants : cinq femmes mariées ainsi que cinq mineurs scolarisés, dont trois jeunes filles de 14 ans et deux garçons de 12 ans.

items.title: COP31 en Turquie: comment financer la transition agricole sur le continent africain?

original_payload.original_title: COP31 en Turquie: comment financer la transition agricole sur le continent africain?
original_payload.original_body:
COP31 en Turquie: comment financer la transition agricole sur le continent africain?
Le COP31, qui s’ouvre ce lundi 9 novembre à Antalya, en Turquie, consacre sa première journée à l’agriculture et pose la question du financement et de l’adaptation au changement climatique des communautés rurales dans les pays en développement.
Publié le :  09/11/2026 - 14:41
2 min     Temps de lecture
Un agriculteur, l'un des 40 ouvriers employés par Nogaye Sene dans son exploitation, ratisse du foin à la périphérie de Joal Fadiout, au Sénégal, ce jeudi 11 décembre 2025.        AP - Caitlin Kelly
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Comment permettre aux petits producteurs qui reçoivent seulement 1 % des financements climats - alors qu'ils fournissent près d'un tiers de l'alimentation mondiale - d'adapter leur outil de travail aux phénomènes climatiques de plus en plus extrêmes ?
Parmi les initiatives lancées à Antalya, 70 millions de dollars ont été mobilisés par le Fonds international de développement agricole (Fida) auprès d’un investisseur japonais. Il s’agit là d’une première obligation dédiée à l’adaptation des communautés rurales au changement climatique qui, selon Diane Menville, directrice financière du Fida, «  permettra d’aller chercher des investisseurs privés pour leur permettre d’investir dans l’adaptation  » au changement climatique.
Selon elle, l’argent promis n’arrive jamais à destination. «  Donc nous, notre rôle, c’est d’essayer de faire le lien entre là où il y a de l’argent et là où il est important d’investir, c’est-à-dire sur le premier kilomètre  », explique Diane Menville, à  Charlotte Cosset  du service économie de RFI.
«  Une question de justice climatique  »
Dans un contexte de baisse drastique de l'aide publique et les taux d'endettement importants, «  on va plaider pour que les mécanismes soient les plus directs possibles  », explique Marie Cosquer, chargée de plaidoyer de l’  ONG   Action contre la faim (ACF). Autrement dit, des fonds d’investissement pourraient lancer des appels à projet pour les organisations de producteurs qui souhaiteraient adapter leurs pratiques au changement climatique. Ce qui permettrait alors que ces fonds puissent arriver directement sur le compte en banque des agriculteurs et «  être contrôlés par un gouvernement ou par une très grosse ONG  », précise Marie Cosquer.
Des méthodes innovantes, donc, qui ont déjà été adoptées par le Gaspi Global Agriculture and Food Security Program, que les   ONG   souhaiteraient voir dupliquer dans les fonds climat.
«  Les financements sont vraiment la pierre angulaire de la plupart des discussions , appuie Marie Cosquer,  ce n’est pas une question de charité, c'est une question de justice climatique.  »
Et pour attirer les investissements du privé dans un secteur considéré comme peu rémunérateur, ACF plaide par exemple pour mieux valoriser les indicateurs comme le gain social ou environnemental dans les choix de production agricole des exploitants.
À lire aussi  «La COP31 ne se déroule pas dans une bulle»: les États réunis à Antalya pour le climat

items.title: Nigeria: l'opposition pourra-t-elle concourir à la présidentielle de janvier?

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria: l'opposition pourra-t-elle concourir à la présidentielle de janvier?
original_payload.original_body:
Nigeria: l'opposition pourra-t-elle concourir à la présidentielle de janvier?
L’opposant Atiku Abubakar, ancien vice-président du Nigeria, pourra-t-il ou non participer à la présidentielle de janvier au Nigéria ? Quelques jours après la décision de la justice d’annuler la candidature de l'opposant le 5 novembre, le Dr Kabiru Sufi, analyste politique basé à Kano, rappelle que cette situation ne concerne pas seulement l’ADC.
Publié le :  09/11/2026 - 13:51   Modifié le :  09/11/2026 - 15:34
2 min     Temps de lecture
Nigéria - la Présidentielle : Des passants passent devant des affiches du président sortant du Nigeria, Bola Tinubu, du Parti du Congrès des progressistes (APC), dans les rues de Lagos, au Nigeria, ce mardi 18 août 2026.        AP Photo/Sunday Alamba - Sunday Alamba
Par :
RFI
Publicité
«  En ce moment, presque tous les principaux partis d’opposition sont en procès  », tient à rappeler d’entrée, Kabiru Sufi, analyste politique nigérian, à notre journaliste du service Afrique  Amélie Tulet . Alors que l’élection présidentielle approche, «  certains partis considèrent que ces crises internes sont orchestrées par des agents du parti au pouvoir  », le Congrès et des progressistes (APC).
C’est notamment le cas du Parti démocratique populaire (PDP) qui, plus tôt dans la semaine, a fait l’objet d’une décision de justice contestée par une frange du parti. La faction dirigée par Abdulrahman Mohammed, considérée comme proche du ministre du Territoire de la capitale fédérale, Nyesom Wike, a été reconnue comme la véritable direction du parti.
À lire aussi  Présidentielle au Nigeria: la justice annule la candidature de l'opposant Atiku Abubakar
«  Une tactique employée par le Congrès des progressistes  (APC, le parti au pouvoir, NDLR)  consiste à judiciariser la politique, en instrumentalisant les tribunaux pour entraver l’opposition  », a dénoncé Kabiru Turaki, président de la faction adverse à celle récemment intronisée, lors d’une conférence de presse dimanche 8 octobre. Un constat partagé par le politologue qui craint que «  tandis que l’APC poursuit ses préparatifs pour les élections  (…)  cela affecte l’opposition et la vie politique nigériane en général  ».
D’autant que le manque de représentativité de l’opposition pourrait créer un déséquilibre politique, mais également régional. Si l’ADC donne du fil à retordre à l’APC, l’absence de candidat du premier dans la course à la présidentielle pourrait en effet déplacer le curseur vers le Congrès démocratique du   Nigeria   (NDC) et son candidat Peter Obi, «  qui est originaire du sud-est  », rappelle Kabiru Sufi : «  Si Atiku n'est pas candidat, la principale opposition sera donc déplacée du nord vers le sud-est  (…)  donc nous aurons deux principaux candidats du sud avec Peter Obi, du sud-est et le président sortant, Bola Tinubu, du sud-ouest.  »
Le reportage de notre correspondant à Abuja, Moïse Gomis, devant le siège de l'ADC
Atiku Abubakar et son parti l'ADC ont entamé les démarches pour faire appel du jugement de la Haute Cour fédérale. Un juge a invalidé jeudi 5 novembre la candidature d'Atiku Abubakar à la présidence, mais aussi de tous les candidats de son parti à tous les échelons. Cette décision fait réagir toute la classe politique au Nigéria. L'APC, le parti du président Tinubu, a déclaré n'avoir joué aucun rôle dans ce différend, soulignant qu'il s'agissait d'une affaire interne au parti, entre les dirigeants de l'ADC.

items.title: Civil servants to buy phones, electronics on interest-free instalments

original_payload.original_title: Civil servants to buy phones, electronics on interest-free instalments
original_payload.original_body:
Metro  Civil servants to buy phones, electronics on interest-free instalments
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   50 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Jumoke Olaitan
Civil servants will soon be able to purchase mobile phones, electronics and household items on interest-free instalments through a new digital marketplace.
The platform, known as FGMarket, is being developed by The Guarantor and Partners Ltd., a digital rent payment and guarantor platform.
The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Mrs Maryam Isah, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday in Abuja.
Isah said The Guarantor and Partners Ltd. was developing FGMarket in collaboration with the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation (OAGF) and the Integrated Payroll and Personnel Information System (IPPIS).
She said the platform would commence operations on Dec. 1, connecting federal civil servants with vendors and manufacturers.
Isah said the initiative was designed to address difficulties workers faced in purchasing essential goods outright, particularly those with limited disposable income.
“Many civil servants have needs that their monthly salaries may not allow them to meet at once.
“The platform is designed to give them the opportunity to acquire essential items and pay over several months,” she said.
She explained that eligible civil servants would be able to select goods online and repay through monthly salary deductions without interest.
“Rather than waiting until they have the full amount to buy an item, workers can access what they need and spread the payments through agreed monthly deductions,” Isah said.
According to her, the arrangement would enable workers to acquire essential items without making full payments upfront or resorting to conventional loans.
She said the platform would feature essential commodities, mobile phones, electronics, household appliances and educational materials, among other products.
Isah explained that interested workers would register using their service numbers and verified phone numbers before undergoing an eligibility verification process.
The CEO said the platform would also provide delivery options, enabling customers to receive purchases at their homes or offices or collect them from designated vendors.
She said the system would give vendors access to a wider market of verified civil servants, while salary deductions would facilitate payment recovery.
“Vendors will also have the opportunity to reach more customers through the platform, while the payment arrangement will provide a structured way for them to receive their money,” she said.
Isah added that the initiative would complement the Federal Government’s efforts to expand access to consumer credit and improve workers’ financial inclusion.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP) was established to expand consumer credit access, particularly among working Nigerians facing difficulties accessing loans.
The corporation is working towards increasing consumer credit access to 50 per cent of economically active Nigerians by 2030.
Isah said FGMarket would support the broader consumer credit initiative by providing workers with a digital channel to access essential goods and spread payments over an agreed period.
She added that consistent repayments through the platform could also help participating workers build credit histories.
“Every time a worker makes a purchase and repays consistently, it contributes to building a record of responsible credit use,” Isah said.
She urged civil servants and vendors to register ahead of the Dec. 1 launch through fgmarket.ng, adding that support was available at the company’s Abuja office.

items.title: FG considers assessment test for Nigerians with foreign degrees before NYSC

original_payload.original_title: FG considers assessment test for Nigerians with foreign degrees before NYSC
original_payload.original_body:
Education  FG considers assessment test for Nigerians with foreign degrees before NYSC
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   11 minutes ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Funmilayo Adeyemi
The Federal Government is considering the introduction of assessment test for Nigerians who obtain degrees from foreign institutions, particularly in African countries.
Dr Folake Olatunji-David, Acting Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, disclosed this at the 37th meeting of the National Standing Committee (NSC) on Evaluation of Foreign Qualifications in Abuja on Monday..
Olatunji-David said the assessment test was necessary before their qualifications would be evaluated for mobilisation into the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC).
She said the proposal was aimed at ensuring that foreign qualifications presented by Nigerians reflected genuine learning achievements and met the required academic standards.
She explained that the measure was particularly important given the increasing number of Nigerians studying in foreign higher institutions, especially in West Africa.
“We must ensure that the standard of education in Nigeria is not lowered by allowing all manner of foreign qualifications that are not recognised, to be paraded by Nigerians without the corresponding learning achievement.
“In as much as we want to encourage global socialisation, education, and the rest of them because the world is a global village now, but we want to maintain standard.
“We want to ensure that, yes, for every certificate given, they are earned, and they can produce people that can contribute positively to our national development.
“I therefore invite this committee once again to consider, if necessary, an assessment test before such graduates are evaluated for NYSC,” she said.
Olatunji-David described the committee as central to efforts to safeguard the integrity of Nigeria’s education system by ensuring that only genuine and duly accredited foreign qualifications were recognised.
She expressed concern over the rising cases of forgery of Nigerian and foreign degree certificates, saying the ministry was taking steps to address the menace.
The acting permanent secretary commended members of the committee for decisions reached at their previous meeting, describing them as important steps towards improving the evaluation and accreditation of foreign qualifications.
She said the ministry had recorded progress in confirming the accreditation status of foreign institutions, issuing clearance letters for NYSC mobilisation, authenticating certificates and issuing no-objection letters.
According to her, the ministry also issues eligibility and proficiency letters to Nigerians traveling abroad for employment or further studies.
“Since the beginning of this year, the evaluation of foreign certificates and authentication of Nigerian certificates have been automated and digitalised, making the process seamless.
“The fees accruing are remitted into government accounts, thereby increasing the ministry’s revenue generation,” Olatunji-David said.
She said the committee would deliberate on five key issues, including guidelines for issuing no-objection letters required for registering proposed institutions with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC).
Others, she said, included compliance by foreign-curriculum secondary schools operating in Nigeria with the country’s education policy on public examinations.
She stressed that such schools must prepare their students for examinations conducted by the West African Examinations Council (WAEC), National Examinations Council (NECO), National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB) or National Board for Arabic and Islamic Studies (NBAIS), as applicable.
According to her, students must sit for at least one of the recognised examinations before graduating from such schools, irrespective of where they intend to pursue higher education.
She said the committee would also consider the recognition of foreign secondary school qualifications, including the Higher School Diploma issued in the United States and Canada, and the Baccalaureate certificates issued by French schools.
She listed other issues for consideration to include establishing mechanisms for monitoring Nigerians studying in African institutions through institutional visits and recognising foreign regulatory bodies responsible for transmitting information on accredited institutions through diplomatic channels.
Earlier, the Director of Education Support Services in the ministry, Mr Gabriel Amudipe , said the committee’s work was critical to improving learning outcomes, institutional performance and quality assurance across the education sector.
Amudipe said the ministry remained committed to evidence-based planning, effective monitoring and transparent evaluation of foreign qualifications.
He urged members to be objective, fair and firm in their deliberations to ensure that genuine qualifications were cleared while cases that fell short of the required standards were appropriately addressed.
“The design and committee on evaluation remains one of the most critical structures for ensuring that our policies, programmes, and interventions are achieved.
“Your work directly influence the improvement of learning outcomes, the strengthening of institutional performance, and the advancement of quality assurance mechanism at all levels of education,” Amudipe said.(NAN)(NAN)

original_payload.original_title: Nigerian artist Ogunyakin elected head of African handicrafts body
original_payload.original_body:
Foreign  Nigerian artist Ogunyakin elected head of African handicrafts body
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   26 minutes ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Damilola Charles
Nigerian artist Opeoluwa Ogunyakin has been elected President of the Organisation for the Development of African Handicrafts (ODEVAA-Africa) for a five-year term.
Nigeria’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Syndoph Endoni, said the development presented an opportunity to strengthen Nigeria’s cultural diplomacy, promote African unity and preserve the continent’s cultural heritage.
This is contained in a statement issued by the Embassy of Nigeria in Ouagadougou and made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN).
Endoni spoke during an engagement with ODEVAA-Africa representatives on the sidelines of the International Arts and Crafts Fair of Ouagadougou.
He urged the organisation’s leadership to protect African arts, traditions and cultural identity while adapting to changing social influences.
The ambassador also called for stronger cooperation among African institutions involved in arts, culture and artisanal development.
He highlighted the economic importance of handicrafts and creative enterprises, noting their contributions to employment and improved livelihoods.
The delegation visited the Nigerian mission partly to celebrate Ogunyakin’s election.
He succeeds Ivorian Ali Cisse, founder and organiser of SIAB, an arts and crafts exhibition in Grand-Bassam, Côte d’Ivoire.
Ogunyakin has more than 30 years’ experience in African arts and crafts.
He is a member of the National Council for Arts and Culture and participated in the 2007 African Festival of Arts and Culture in Abuja.
He previously served as President of ODEVAA Nigeria and is Chief Executive Officer of Artminds and Décor.
ODEVAA-Africa promotes African arts and heritage and supports employment opportunities for youths, women and persons living with disabilities.
The organisation operates in more than 28 African countries through national presidents and membership networks.
Representatives from Ghana, The Gambia, Burkina Faso, Benin Republic, Togo, Cameroon, Guinea and Côte d’Ivoire attended the meeting.
The Nigerian mission said Ogunyakin’s emergence could strengthen Nigeria’s engagement in artisanal development, education, science and technology across Africa.
It added that closer engagement with ODEVAA-Africa would require institutional partnerships, capacity building and practical support for African-led initiatives to advance continental integration and economic cooperation. (NAN)
Edited by Tosin Kolade

items.title: AUPCTRE, water groups urge parties to prioritise universal water access

original_payload.original_title: AUPCTRE, water groups urge parties to prioritise universal water access
original_payload.original_body:
Environment  AUPCTRE, water groups urge parties to prioritise universal water access
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   28 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Eniola Elewude
The Amalgamated Union of Public Corporations Civil Service Technical and Recreational Services Employees (  AUPCTRE)   and water advocacy groups have urged political parties to prioritise universal access to safe water ahead of the 2027 elections.
They also called on the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to provide an update on the implementation of its 2023 campaign promise to improve access to clean water across the country by 2030.
The  News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)  reports that the APC’s Renewed Hope Manifesto aims to ensure that, by 2030, every Nigerian lives within a five-minute walk of a clean water source.
The groups made the call in a statement issued in Abuja on Monday after a meeting with the newly elected national executives of AUPCTRE, led by its National President, Eugene Manji.
The statement was signed by Philip Jakpor, Executive Director of Renevlyn Development Initiative (RDI).
Other groups involved included the Citizens Free Service Forum (CFSF), Ecumenical Water Network (EWN) Africa, Child Health Organisation (CHO), Environmental Defenders Network (EDEN) and New Life Community Care Initiative (NELCCI).
They expressed concern that political parties had given little attention to access to safe water in their campaign promises, in spite of the country’s water supply challenges.
The groups cited global data indicating that access to clean water in Nigeria stood at about 29.9 per cent, attributing the slow progress in the sector partly to institutional fragmentation at federal and state levels.
They said the challenges were documented in a 2025 report, ‘Dry Taps: A Damning Verdict on the State of Water Utilities in Nigeria’, which examined water utilities in Oyo, Lagos, Kogi, Enugu, Edo and Kano states.
According to them, the report showed that years of neglect by federal and state governments had left many water utilities operating below capacity, forcing residents to depend on costly and potentially unsafe alternatives.
The statement quoted Manji as saying millions of Nigerians still relied on unsafe water sources, while those who could afford commercially supplied water paid heavily for it.
He warned that the situation exposed citizens to waterborne diseases and possible contamination from harmful chemicals.
Similarly, CFSF Executive Director, Sani Baba, said political parties had yet to present convincing plans to address the country’s water crisis.
Baba urged Nigerians to demand clear commitments on universal water access from political parties seeking electoral support.
Jakpor said water was fundamental to food security, energy, public health and climate resilience and should therefore feature prominently in political parties’ development plans.
The groups also opposed the proposed private-sector takeover of publicly funded state water corporations, especially the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model being promoted by the Lagos State Government.
They urged political parties to consider the Public-Public Partnership (PuP) model, which involves collaboration among public and non-profit organisations to provide services, develop infrastructure and share technical expertise.
They also called for improved workers’ welfare, decent working conditions and fair wages to address the economic challenges facing water sector employees. (NAN)

original_payload.original_body:
General News  Ondo: Aroloye’s emergence as Owa-elect significant milestone in Idanre Kingdom—Stakeholder
By  Chijioke Okoronkwo   ·   55 minutes ago   ·  3 min read
Prince Mayowa Aroloye
✓
✓
Prince Mayowa Aroloye
By Daniel Obaje
Mr Samuel Afolabi, a prominent stakeholder in Ondo State’s Idanre Kingdom, has described the emergence of Prince Mayowa Aroloye as the Owa-elect as a remarkable milestone in the ancient kingdom’s history.
Afolabi, who is the General Secretary of the Prince Mayowa Toluade Aroloye (PMA) Obaship Movement, shared these reflections in a memoir made available to newsmen on Monday in Abuja.
Afolabi said that the election of Aroloye as the new Owa of Idanre Kingdom during the keenly contested selection process on Nov. 3 represented an extraordinary moment in the traditional history of the land.
He noted that the outcome brought a rigorous succession process to a peaceful close while opening a fresh chapter for the revered traditional institution.
According to him, Aroloye’s ascension to the throne carried deep historical weight because it is directly tied to the noble heritage and enduring legacy of his late father, Oba Fredrick Aroloye.
“He is a direct biological son of the late Aroloye, the immediate past paramount ruler of Idanre Kingdom.
“His father was one of the most historically significant monarchs in the recent traditional history of Idanre Kingdom, having ascended the throne in 1976 and reigned for 48 remarkable years until his demise on July 30, 2024.’’
Afolabi highlighted a journey defined by both global exposure and Aroloye’s deep commitment to his roots.
“Born in Odode-Idanre, Aroloye pursued his education and built an impressive career spanning professional engagements, business investments, and humanitarian initiatives across both Nigeria and the United Kingdom.’’
He said that in spite of his international exposure and achievements abroad, Aroloye never lost sight of his heritage.
“Following the passing of his father in July 2024, he returned to his ancestral homeland to answer the call of duty and participate in the traditional succession process.
“His life reflects the journey of a prince who, having experienced different dimensions of life, returned to his ancestral homeland to participate in the succession process following the demise of his illustrious father.’’
He said that the Owa-elect’s background adequately equipped him to bridge the gap between traditional customs and modern governance.
According to the general-secretary, Aroloye’s emergence goes far beyond a personal victory or family triumph.
He described Aroloye’s election as a pivotal moment in the ongoing story of Idanre land, noting that it served to strengthen its royal institution and preserve its rich historical identity for future generations.
Afolabi expressed confidence that the Owa-elect would uphold the dignity of the Aroloye lineage as Idanre Kingdom prepared for the formal coronation and transition of power.( NAN )

items.title: Pate calls for harmonised health training standards across ECOWAS

original_payload.original_title: Pate calls for harmonised health training standards across ECOWAS
original_payload.original_body:
Health  Pate calls for harmonised health training standards across ECOWAS
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   1 hour ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
⁠⁠​‍‍⁠⁠‍‍​‌‍⁠​‌‍‌​  By Franca Ofili
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Pate, has called for harmonised health training standards across ECOWAS member states to strengthen regional integration and improve healthcare delivery.
Pate made the call in Abuja on Monday at the Integration Meeting of Accredited West African Colleges, Training Institutions and Regulatory Bodies in the ECOWAS region.
Represented by Dr Dakum Londji, Nigeria’s Liaison Officer to WAHO/African Union at the ministry, he said diseases does not respect national borders, stressing that solutions, knowledge and health professionals must equally move freely across the region.
He noted that strong healthcare systems required a competent workforce, supported by quality and harmonised education and training standards across West Africa.
The minister observed that differences in curricula, training standards and accreditation processes had limited professional mobility, weakened quality and restricted health workers’ opportunities to practise across the region.
He said the meeting provided an opportunity to address the challenges through common standards of excellence while respecting the national contexts of ECOWAS member states.
He identified harmonisation of curricula and standards, mutual recognition of qualifications and professional mobility, as well as quality assurance and accountability as key priorities.
“Member states must agree on core competencies, minimum training standards and common accreditation criteria for health training colleges and educational institutions.
“Mutual recognition of qualifications will enable doctors, midwives and other health professionals trained in one ECOWAS country to practise confidently and credibly across the region,” he said.
Pate also called for stronger collaboration among regulatory bodies to promote data sharing, enforce professional ethics and ensure graduates were competent, compassionate and fit for practice.
He said the initiative aligned with Nigeria’s Renewed Hope Agenda and ongoing health sector reforms, which focused on strengthening training institutions, expanding accreditation and improving professional regulation.
He added that Nigeria was also promoting digital learning and innovation to strengthen health professional education and improve the quality of healthcare delivery.
He described regional integration as a necessity rather than an option, urging stakeholders to adopt practical decisions and develop a clear roadmap with timelines for implementation.
The minister commended WAHO, the ECOWAS commission, regulatory bodies, training institutions and development partners for their contributions to strengthening health professional education across the region.
He expressed optimism that the deliberations would produce actionable decisions to advance harmonisation and regional cooperation.( NAN )

items.title: Handball – Championnat amateur Matanti 2026 : L’ASPAC réalise le doublé et s’offre les deux couronnes

original_payload.original_title: Handball – Championnat amateur Matanti 2026 : L’ASPAC réalise le doublé et s’offre les deux couronnes
original_payload.original_body:
L’Association sportive du port autonome de Cotonou (ASPAC) a signé une performance remarquable au Championnat amateur Matanti 2026 de handball. À l’issue des finales disputées le mercredi 4 novembre au Hall des Arts, Loisirs et Sports de Cotonou, les formations masculine et féminine du club portuaire ont dominé leurs homologues d’Espoir pour s’adjuger les deux trophées.
‎Jéconias ADANLE (Coll)
L’ASPAC a dicté sa loi sur les parquets du Hall des Arts, Loisirs et Sports de Cotonou. Engagées dans les deux finales du Championnat amateur Matanti 2026, les équipes masculine et féminine du club portuaire ont répondu présentes, offrant à leur formation une double consécration face à Espoir. ‎Chez les dames, les Portuaires ont ouvert le bal des victoires en s’imposant sur le score de 28-22. Opposées à une équipe d’Espoir déterminée, les joueuses de l’ASPAC ont fait preuve de maîtrise, de solidité et d’efficacité pour prendre le dessus. Une victoire qui récompense les efforts consentis tout au long de la compétition et leur permet de décrocher le titre féminin.
Dans la catégorie masculine, l’ASPAC a également tenu son rang. Face à Espoir, les hommes ont livré une prestation convaincante pour s’imposer 26-22. Portés notamment par une défense bien organisée, les joueurs ont su faire la différence pour offrir au club son deuxième trophée de la journée. L’ASPAC repart ainsi de cette édition 2026 avec les deux couronnes en jeu. ‎Au coup de sifflet final, la satisfaction était naturellement au rendez-vous dans le camp portuaire. Capitaine de l’ASPAC HBC hommes, Olaoumi Mahafouz n’a pas caché son émotion après cette consécration. « Je suis très heureux, je ne sais même pas comment exprimer ma joie. C’est une victoire qu’on voulait depuis. On a toujours travaillé sur notre défense. Le coach nous disait toujours, si on va gagner, c’est notre défense », a-t-il confié.
Matanti et la Fédération béninoise de handball au rendez-vous
Au-delà des enjeux sportifs, ces finales ont également été marquées par des initiatives en faveur du développement de la discipline. À la mi-temps de chacune des deux rencontres, la Fédération béninoise de handball a procédé à une remise de 500 ballons destinés aux classes sportives inscrites dans le cadre du Programme de promotion et de développement des activités sportives (PPDAS). À travers cette action, l’instance fédérale entend renforcer la pratique du handball à la base et améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage et de formation des jeunes talents.
Une initiative qui témoigne de l’importance accordée à la relève dans la construction de l’avenir du handball béninois. ‎La cérémonie a également été l’occasion de présenter au public le trophée remporté par la sélection nationale senior féminine lors du Tournoi international de Smara, au Maroc. Les Amazones ont conservé leur couronne grâce à un parcours sans faute, ponctué de trois victoires en autant de rencontres. Leur dernier succès, obtenu face au Canada sur le score de 24-21, est venu confirmer leur performance dans cette compétition.
Des satisfactions partagées pour l’avenir du handball béninois
La représentante de Matanti a, pour sa part, exprimé sa satisfaction quant à cette collaboration avec la Fédération béninoise de handball. « Nous sommes heureux de collaborer avec vous. C’est un plaisir pour nous de participer au championnat que vous organisez chaque année », a-t-elle déclaré, réaffirmant ainsi l’engagement du partenaire aux côtés de la discipline. Représentant la Fédération béninoise de handball, le deuxième vice-président, Fortuné Guédou, a également salué le niveau des prestations offertes par les différentes formations. Selon lui, les équipes engagées ont démontré, à travers leurs performances, les progrès réalisés dans le championnat amateur. «Les différentes équipes ont montré que du concret se fait sur le terrain.
Le niveau de chaque année évolue. C’est l’occasion de remercier tous les acteurs qui soutiennent le comité exécutif dans la tâche qu’il accomplit », a-t-il souligné. Il a par ailleurs félicité les clubs pour le bon déroulement de la compétition, insistant sur l’esprit de convivialité qui a caractérisé cette phase finale. « Tout s’est déroulé encore comme en famille. Merci à Matanti qui a soutenu cette phase finale du championnat amateur », a-t-il ajouté. ‎Avec le doublé de l’ASPAC, la dotation de 500 ballons au profit des classes sportives et la présentation du trophée continental remporté par les Amazones à Smara, les finales du Championnat amateur Matanti 2026 auront été riches en enseignements et en satisfactions.

items.title: Inclusion numérique : AS World Tech lance « Étudiants Connectés » avec l’ambition d’équiper 100 000 étudiants

original_payload.original_title: Inclusion numérique : AS World Tech lance « Étudiants Connectés » avec l’ambition d’équiper 100 000 étudiants
original_payload.original_body:
À travers son programme « Étudiants Connectés », présenté le lundi 9 novembre 2026 à Wegal Space, à Cotonou, AS World Tech ambitionne de faciliter l’accès des étudiants béninois aux équipements informatiques et aux services numériques. Un dispositif reposant sur l’acquisition d’ordinateurs à crédit, auquel s’ajoutent des offres de connexion Internet, de cybersécurité et d’assistance technique.
Faire de l’accès à l’outil informatique un levier de formation, de compétitivité et d’insertion professionnelle pour la jeunesse béninoise. C’est l’ambition affichée par AS World Tech à travers le programme « Étudiants Connectés », officiellement présenté à la presse ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, à Wegal Space, à Cotonou. A cette occasion, le Directeur général de AS World Tech, Richard Odjrado, a exposé la genèse et les ambitions de cette initiative mûrie pendant trois années. L’objectif, à l’en croire, est de mettre progressivement 100 000 ordinateurs à la disposition de 100 000 étudiants béninois, afin de réduire les difficultés d’accès aux équipements informatiques et de favoriser leur participation à la transformation numérique.
Deux modèles mis en avant
Inscrit dans le programme plus large « Bénin Connecté », « Étudiants Connectés » repose sur un mécanisme de financement destiné à rendre l’acquisition d’un ordinateur moins contraignante pour les étudiants. AS World Tech annonce un paiement échelonné sur 24 mois. Deux modèles d’ordinateurs sont proposés. Le premier, dénommé FIFA R, constitue l’offre d’entrée de gamme. Affiché à 170 000 FCFA, il est destiné aux étudiants dont les activités académiques ne nécessitent pas de grandes performances informatiques. L’accès à ce modèle prévoit une avance annoncée entre 20 000 et 50 000 FCFA, puis des mensualités de 7 000 FCFA pendant deux ans.
Le second modèle, plus performant, est équipé d’un processeur Intel Core i7 de 13è génération, d’un disque SSD de 1 To et d’une mémoire vive de 32 Go. Le directeur général a évoqué un prix de marché d’environ 860 000 FCFA, avec une tarification préférentielle dans le cadre du programme. Les modalités présentées prévoient une avance de 70 000 FCFA et des mensualités de 23 000 FCFA sur 24 mois.
Trois profils d’étudiants pris en compte
Pour les étudiants boursiers, un mécanisme de remboursement à partir de la bourse et du compte domicilié à La Poste du Bénin a été étudié. La question de la perte éventuelle de la bourse est également prise en compte, avec la possibilité de recourir à un souscripteur garant. Les étudiants non boursiers pourront, quant à eux, bénéficier de l’engagement financier d’un parent ou d’une autre personne disposée à garantir le remboursement. Pour les étudiants sans soutien financier, AS World Tech annonce un mécanisme développé avec son partenaire MTN.
Il s’agira de permettre aux bénéficiaires de gagner des points et des revenus à travers le partage de liens et la recommandation de produits ou de services sur les réseaux sociaux et les plateformes numériques. Selon Richard Odjrado, ce dispositif pourrait permettre à certains étudiants de générer jusqu’à 600 000 FCFA de revenus. Le programme sera toutefois déployé progressivement. Une première phase portera sur 2 000 ordinateurs, avant une montée en puissance vers l’objectif global de 100 000 équipements.
Internet, cybersécurité et assistance technique
Au-delà de la fourniture d’ordinateurs, l’initiative entend proposer un environnement numérique plus complet. Une offre de connexion Internet illimitée est annoncée à 10 000 FCFA par mois, avec une possibilité de paiement fractionné au quotidien. L’accès prévoit une avance initiale annoncée entre 5 000 FCFA. A cela s’ajoute une offre de cybersécurité développée avec Kaspersky, présentée à 1 700 FCFA par mois, soit 20 000 FCFA par an. Le promoteur annonce également un dispositif de service après-vente disponible 24 heures sur 24 et 7 jours sur 7, ainsi qu’une couverture d’assurance prévoyant notamment le remplacement de l’ordinateur en cas de vol, sous réserve des vérifications et conditions applicables.
Le directeur des opérations, Marius Houndenou, a, pour sa part, insisté sur les motivations profondes du projet. Il a notamment évoqué la nécessité de faciliter l’accès à la formation et aux opportunités internationales, afin que les jeunes Béninois puissent rivaliser avec leurs homologues d’autres pays. Pour lui, la démocratisation de l’équipement informatique doit permettre de révéler des talents encore inexploités et de lever les barrières qui empêchent certains jeunes de participer pleinement à la révolution numérique.
Intervenant également au cours de la rencontre, la chargée des médias et animatrice, Majoie Houndji, a partagé son expérience avec un ordinateur de marque AS qu’elle utilise depuis plus de quatre ans, après avoir procédé au remplacement de son écran.

items.title: 4e anniversaire de son ordination sacerdotale : Le Prophète Malachie prie pour les défunts et soutient la candidate Juliana Lumumba

original_payload.original_title: 4e anniversaire de son ordination sacerdotale : Le Prophète Malachie prie pour les défunts et soutient la candidate Juliana Lumumba
original_payload.original_body:
À l’occasion du quatrième anniversaire de son ordination sacerdotale à la paroisse Temidiri Ilara Imeko, le Prophète Malachie (Antoine Tycko Odjo) a réuni ce week-end un collège de dignitaires religieux du Bénin et du Nigeria. Entre rituels d’intercession pour les parents défunts thème central de cette commémoration inspiré des Écritures et ferveur spirituelle autour de sa marraine Juliana Lumumba Amato, candidate au secrétariat général de la Francophonie, l’événement a mêlé devoir de mémoire et prophétie internationale.
IQuatre ans de mission, quatre ans d’espérance. C’est dans cette atmosphère de bilan et de dévotion que les fidèles de l’Église des Chérubins et des Séraphins se sont rassemblés ce week-end à la Paroisse Temidiri Ilara Imeko, à la frontière bénino-nigériane Le Matinal. L’ancien journaliste béninois Antoine Tycko Odjo Le Matinal, aujourd’hui connu sous le nom de Prophète Malachie, y célébrait quatre années de sacerdoce intense. Un parcours que l’homme de Dieu place sous le signe des aspirations profondes et de la fidélité aux préceptes divins.
L’intercession pour les défunts : un appel contre l’oubli et une loi de semence
Le point d’orgue spirituel de cette célébration est venu bousculer les consciences sur une réalité trop souvent occultée : la négligence des ancêtres et des parents disparus. Le Prophète Malachie a articulé ses enseignements autour d’un thème sans équivoque : « Aider nos défunts par notre prière d’intercession », tiré du livre biblique de 2 Maccabées 12, 45.
Pour le célébrant, se souvenir de ses parents défunts n’est pas une option, mais un devoir sacré lié à une loi spirituelle de réciprocité. Face aux fidèles, le Prophète Malachie a insisté sur cette vérité immuable : « Sachez que ce que l’on sème pour ses parents, nos enfants nous le rendent un jour. C’est le cycle de la vie, et vos enfants sauront vous honorer de la même manière. »
Au-delà du geste traditionnel d’allumer des bougies, des rituels réservés et des prières spécifiques ont été rigoureusement exécutés au cours des cérémonies de ce week-end. Plusieurs personnalités de haut rang, ayant placé leur confiance dans l’appel du prophète, ont ainsi vu la mémoire de leurs proches honorée à travers des liturgies d’intercession visant à apaiser et accompagner les âmes de l’autre côté du voile.
Le sort de la Francophonie entre les mains du Divin
Si la commémoration regardait vers le ciel et le passé, elle s’est aussi résolument ancrée dans les grands défis du présent et de la diplomatie internationale. Le rayonnement de ce quatrième anniversaire s’est matérialisé par le choix d’une marraine d’envergure, Juliana Lumumba Amato, candidate au poste de Secrétaire général de la Francophonie Radio-Canada. En la plaçant au cœur de cette commémoration, l’Église unit la force de la prière aux ambitions d’excellence de cette haute figure africaine.
Preuve de la dimension transfrontalière et de la portée de cet événement, un collège de prophètes venus du Bénin et du Nigeria a officiellement pris la décision d’escorter spirituellement Juliana Lumumba Amato dans sa quête. Par cette alliance mystique et fraternelle, la paroisse Temidiri Ilara Imeko s’impose non seulement comme un sanctuaire de foi, mais aussi comme le point de départ d’une dynamique spirituelle d’envergure africaine et internationale.

items.title: Western Equatoria prepares election officials for polls

original_payload.original_title: Western Equatoria prepares election officials for polls
original_payload.original_body:
The Western Equatoria State government, in collaboration with the State High Elections Committee (SHEC), on Monday launched a two-day induction training for constituency returning officers and assistant constituency returning officers in Yambio.
The training is intended to equip the officials with the knowledge and skills needed to coordinate electoral activities and support preparations for the forthcoming elections across the state.
Speaking at the opening ceremony, Western Equatoria State Caretaker Governor Badagbu Daniel Rimbasa reaffirmed the government’s commitment to providing security and logistical support for the electoral process.
Rimbasa also pledged to facilitate electricity connectivity by Tuesday to support the committee’s operations.
He urged participants to take the training seriously and pass on the knowledge and skills acquired to other electoral personnel in their respective constituencies through a Training of Trainers (ToT) approach.
The governor said the officials had an important role in strengthening electoral preparations at the grassroots level by sharing their knowledge and training other personnel in their communities.
He said the people of South Sudan had waited a long time for an opportunity to elect their leaders, adding that the national leadership had resolved to give citizens the chance to choose their representatives through the ballot.
SHEC Chairperson Simon Bakama said the two-day training was designed to prepare constituency returning officers and their assistants for their responsibilities ahead of the forthcoming electoral activities.
Bakama said the training would provide participants with the knowledge and practical skills needed to coordinate electoral activities, support registration officers and ensure that personnel assigned to designated registration centres were adequately prepared for their duties.
He added that the officials would also be responsible for supporting and training registration officers in their respective constituencies and counties to strengthen the voter registration process.
The officials are expected to serve across Western Equatoria State’s 10 counties: Yambio, Nzara, Ibba, Maridi, Mvolo, Mundri East, Mundri West, Ezo, Tambura and Nagero.
The training is expected to strengthen the capacity of electoral personnel and improve coordination of electoral activities across the state ahead of the forthcoming elections.

items.title: Media Authority warns against hate speech ahead of elections

original_payload.original_title: Media Authority warns against hate speech ahead of elections
original_payload.original_body:
South Sudan’s Media Authority has warned politicians, their supporters and social media users against spreading hate speech and inflammatory messages, saying those involved in unlawful conduct could face legal action as the country approaches the December polls.
Addressing a press conference in Juba on Monday, Ajuo Luol Akuai, the managing director of the Media Authority, said they have observed increasing signs of harmful and inflammatory communication across digital platforms, raising concerns about its potential impact on public peace, national cohesion and the credibility of the electoral process.
He said the development had prompted the Authority to remind candidates and media practitioners of their responsibilities in promoting peaceful electoral discussions and responsible communication.
“The Authority reminds political candidates, their supporters, media practitioners, social media users and the general public that peaceful elections are a shared national responsibility,” the statement reads in part. “Political campaigns should provide an opportunity for constructive debate, democratic participation and the exchange of ideas, rather than platforms for promoting hatred, division, intimidation or violence.”
Luol said the authority registered some cases of hate speech mainly by online pages belonging to some political parties in Jonglei, Upper Nile and Equatoria regions respectively.
He urged candidates and their supporters to conduct peaceful campaigns, respect opposing views and refrain from inflammatory statements or communications that could threaten public peace and stability.
The Media Authority also called on journalists and media houses to uphold professional and ethical journalism, stressing the importance of accuracy and impartiality in reporting.
“Information must be verified before publication, and media platforms should not be used to amplify hate speech, unverified claims, or content that could incite violence,” Luol stated.
He further encouraged social media users and digital-content creators to exercise responsibility when creating and sharing information.
The Authority said it would continue monitoring media content and collaborate with relevant institutions to address violations within its mandate.
“Individuals and media entities engaging in unlawful conduct may face applicable legal or regulatory consequences in accordance with the law and due process,” he said.
The Media Authority also announced plans to launch a public awareness campaign to combat hate speech, misinformation and disinformation during the electoral period, subject to the availability of necessary resources and support.
The Authority called on all stakeholders to promote responsible communication and peaceful public engagement throughout the electoral cycle, from civic education and political campaigns to voting, the announcement of results and the post-election period.
“No political ambition or personal interest should come at the expense of the lives, safety, and unity of our people,” Luol concluded. “Let us use our voices and communication platforms responsibly, reject messages that divide our communities, and work together to ensure peaceful, credible, and inclusive elections.”

items.title: Haroun’s appearance puts Sudan’s military in awkward position, lawyer says

original_payload.original_title: Haroun’s appearance puts Sudan’s military in awkward position, lawyer says
original_payload.original_body:
The public appearance of Ahmed Haroun, chairman of Sudan’s former ruling National Congress Party (NCP), has put the country’s military authorities in  an uncomfortable position , raising questions about their handling of his case, the influence of former regime figures and the independence of judicial institutions, Sudanese lawyer Muaz Hadra has said.
Speaking to Radio Tamazuj about the legal and political implications of Haroun’s recent public appearances, Hadra said Monday that the former official faces criminal charges before Sudanese courts relating to war crimes and crimes against humanity, offences that are not eligible for release on ordinary bail.
“These are war crimes and crimes against humanity,” Hadra said, adding that Haroun is also wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Darfur in the early 2000s. Haroun has denied the charges, describing them as politically motivated.
Hadra said Haroun was initially detained under the former transitional government but left prison amid the security breakdown following the outbreak of war in April 2023. Haroun escaped from Kober Prison in April 2024 after the facility was attacked during fighting between the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
Questioning why Haroun had not returned to prison despite being at large for more than two years, Hadra said: “So why did he not return to prison? This is the question.”
Military’s handling questioned
Hadra questioned the circumstances surrounding Haroun’s detention on Sunday by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), arguing that the military was not the appropriate institution to handle his arrest and detention.
“The army is not the institution that should arrest Ahmed Haroun. He should be arrested by the police and the judicial authorities because he is facing criminal charges. The army has nothing to do with him,” Hadra said.
He argued that the military’s involvement suggested Haroun could be held at a secure location under military protection rather than being subjected to ordinary judicial procedures.
“This shows that they want to protect him in a safe place, as they did with al-Bashir, Abdel Rahim Mohamed Hussein and others,” he said, referring to former president Omar al-Bashir and former defence minister Abdel Rahim Mohamed Hussein.
NCP influence resurfaces
Hadra said Haroun’s media appearances and public statements demonstrated the continued influence of the former ruling NCP, suggesting that the disbanded party was moving from operating discreetly to openly asserting its political presence.
He said Haroun had criticised various political actors, the December 2018 revolution that led to al-Bashir’s removal from power in April 2019, and the armed forces.
Although Haroun had not directly criticised army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, Hadra said some of his remarks amounted to indirect criticism of the military leadership. He argued that Haroun appeared to suggest that Burhan had protected individuals who had betrayed the former ruling party.
Describing the shift in the party’s public posture, Hadra said: “He used to be secretive, but now he is public.”
Regional and international implications
Hadra said Haroun’s public appearance had created an uncomfortable situation for the authorities in their relations with neighbouring countries, particularly Saudi Arabia and Egypt.
“This is a big embarrassment for the government, especially towards some of its neighbours, such as Saudi Arabia, Egypt and others,” he said.
He argued that the development could undermine efforts by the authorities to distance themselves from the former ruling party and its Islamist networks, amid regional concerns about the possible restoration of political influence by figures associated with al-Bashir’s government.
Hadra also pointed to international pressure over Haroun’s outstanding ICC case, citing a $5 million reward offered by the United States for information leading to his capture.
The US State Department has accused Haroun of recruiting, financing and arming the Janjaweed militia, which was implicated in atrocities in Darfur, including killings, rape, torture and forced displacement.
Hadra expressed doubt that the military leadership would cooperate with US efforts to secure Haroun’s arrest, arguing that senior figures within the armed forces remained closely aligned with the former ruling NCP.
“I don’t think the army is cooperating with the United States because the army leadership is completely aligned with the National Congress Party,” he said.
Accountability concerns
Hadra said the circumstances surrounding Haroun’s public appearance and detention raised broader questions about the relationship between the military establishment and former ruling party figures, as well as the prospects for accountability.
He argued that close ties between senior military figures and former NCP officials could undermine efforts to establish independent judicial institutions and ensure accountability for crimes committed under the previous government.
The case, he said, placed the independence of Sudan’s judicial institutions and the prospects for transitional justice under scrutiny as the country continues to grapple with war and political instability.

items.title: Tchad : face au déficit des pluies, le gouvernement mise sur les cultures de contre-saison et l’irrigation

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : face au déficit des pluies, le gouvernement mise sur les cultures de contre-saison et l’irrigation
original_payload.original_body:
À l’Assemblée nationale, ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, le ministre de la Production et de l’Industrialisation agricole, Keda Ballah, a présenté les mesures destinées à soutenir les producteurs confrontés à une campagne agricole perturbée. Semences, intrants, forages solaires et renforcement de l’encadrement figurent parmi les réponses annoncées, sur fond de volonté de réduire la dépendance de l’agriculture aux pluies.
Des semis tardifs, des pluies irrégulières et des séquences sèches au moment où les cultures avaient besoin d’eau : devant les députés réunis sous la présidence d’Ali Kolotou Tchaïmi, Keda Ballah a dressé le constat d’une campagne agricole 2026-2027 éprouvante pour les producteurs tchadiens.
Selon le ministre, la mauvaise répartition des précipitations dans le temps et dans l’espace a affecté les pâturages ainsi que le développement des cultures vivrières, notamment au stade de la floraison. Une situation qu’il attribue au dérèglement climatique et présente comme une préoccupation majeure du gouvernement.
Pour mesurer les conséquences de ce choc, une mission réunissant plusieurs ministres, des responsables techniques et des partenaires internationaux a parcouru onze provinces fortement touchées. Conduite par le ministre d’État chargé des Finances, elle a débouché, selon Keda Ballah, sur des actions à court et à moyen terme dont la mise en œuvre incombe aux différents départements concernés.
Face aux questions des députés sur l’aide aux producteurs, le ministre a voulu distinguer les moyens immédiatement mobilisables des commandes en cours.
» Je préfère dire ce qui est concret plutôt que de rester sur les projections « , a-t-il déclaré avant de détailler les stocks et les approvisionnements annoncés.
Lire aussi  :  Irrégularité des pluies : « Cette situation nous rappelle que le climat devient plus variable », Dr Allaramadji Mouldjidé, Géographe
Pour les cultures de contre-saison, six tonnes de semences de riz sont disponibles, selon son exposé. À cela s’ajoutent quinze tonnes de semences maraîchères apportées par la FAO pour le Barh El Gazel, le Kanem, le Batha et le Ouaddaï. Oignon, piment, gombo, carotte, pastèque et tomate figurent parmi les cultures concernées. Trois mille kits maraîchers sont également annoncés comme disponibles pour ces provinces.
Le ministre a aussi fait état d’une commande de 5 000 tonnes de semences, principalement de sorgho et de maïs, passée à travers le projet Pérensa. Il a précisé qu’une partie de cette commande concernait le maraîchage et que ces approvisionnements devaient également contribuer à préparer la prochaine campagne.
Le ministre a défendu une mobilisation plus importante des ressources hydriques souterraines et des terres propices aux cultures de contre-saison. Pour lui, la sécurité alimentaire ne peut être appréciée à travers la seule pluviométrie.
Lire aussi  :  Irrégularité des pluies : ‘’Nous restons pleinement mobilisés aux côtés de nos concitoyens’’, Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno
Concernant les engrais, Keda Ballah a annoncé la disponibilité de 380 tonnes de NPK dans les douze provinces couvertes par le projet 3Agri. Dix tonnes supplémentaires sont, selon lui, en cours de commande, avec une livraison attendue dans un délai maximal de trois mois.
Il a par ailleurs évoqué le projet d’usine d’engrais dont la première pierre vient d’être posée. D’après les engagements de l’investisseur rapportés devant les députés, la production d’engrais organo-minéraux pourrait commencer dès avril prochain, avec un objectif annuel annoncé de 176 000 tonnes. Cette perspective reste toutefois distincte des moyens déjà disponibles pour répondre aux difficultés actuelles.
Le ministre a néanmoins reconnu deux difficultés : la diffusion rapide des alertes et la mobilisation des ressources nécessaires aux interventions d’urgence.

items.title: Logone oriental : des groupements féminins dotés de kits de sensibilisation

original_payload.original_title: Logone oriental : des groupements féminins dotés de kits de sensibilisation
original_payload.original_body:
La délégation provinciale de la Femme et de la Petite Enfance du Logone oriental, avec l’appui de l’UNICEF, a procédé, ce 9 novembre 2026 à Doba, à la remise de kits aux associations et groupements féminins venus des six départements que compte la province.
Ces kits sont composés de soixante tapis de six places et de trente-huit baffles équipés de micros baladeurs. Ils sont destinés aux femmes issues de trente associations et groupements féminins. Ce geste vise à soutenir ces femmes dans leurs campagnes de sensibilisation au sein de leurs localités respectives sur les droits de la femme, la protection de l’enfant et la prévention des pratiques néfastes, notamment le mariage d’enfants, le viol et les mutilations génitales féminines.
La déléguée provinciale de la Femme et de la Petite enfance du Logone oriental, Yodamné Marie, a indiqué que ces matériels de sonorisation et ces tapis ont été remis aux bénéficiaires pour leur permettre d’organiser des rencontres de sensibilisation et d’échanges autour des problématiques liées aux droits des femmes, à leur protection, à la prévention des pratiques néfastes et à la lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes.
Lire aussi :  Logone oriental : des femmes formées aux droits et à la protection de l’enfant
De leur côté, les bénéficiaires ont unanimement remercié la délégation de la Femme et l’UNICEF pour cet appui. Elles promettent de traduire dans les faits les connaissances acquises lors de la formation et d’utiliser à bon scient ces kits pour leurs activités de sensibilisation.
Il faut signaler que cette remise intervient après deux jours de formation sur les droits et la protection de l’enfant ainsi que sur la prévention des pratiques néfastes.
Tolobé Mbaïnaïssem Dieudonné, correspondant à Doba

items.title: France : le judoka Teddy Riner annonce sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle de 2027

original_payload.original_title: France : le judoka Teddy Riner annonce sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle de 2027
original_payload.original_body:
Le triple champion olympique de judo, Teddy Riner, annonce sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle française de 2027. À 37 ans, le champion entend se positionner en dehors des clivages politiques traditionnels, avec l’ambition de devenir un « président qui fédère » et de rassembler les Français.
Dans un entretien accordé au journal Le Parisien, Teddy Riner a dévoilé les motivations de son engagement politique. Se présentant comme un candidat « ni à droite ni à gauche », il affirme vouloir proposer une autre voie politique, fondée sur le rassemblement et le dépassement des divisions partisanes.
« Je suis candidat à l’élection présidentielle de 2027. Aujourd’hui, on vit côte à côte, je crains que demain on doive vivre face à face », a-t-il déclaré.
Le champion olympique dresse un constat préoccupant de la situation du pays, évoquant notamment la montée de la peur, le renoncement et le sentiment d’abandon qui toucheraient une partie de la population.
« Regardez notre pays, regardez nos rues, nos campagnes, nos quartiers. On a laissé s’installer la peur, le renoncement et un sentiment d’abandon généralisé », a-t-il souligné.
Pour Teddy Riner, la France n’a pas besoin d’un professionnel de la politique, mais d’un leadership axé sur le bon sens, la fermeté et la justice.
Pour concrétiser cette ambition, le judoka lance également son site internet de campagne, baptisé « La France qu’on veut », et appelle les citoyens qui partagent sa vision à rejoindre son mouvement.

items.title: RDC : 65 militaires condamnés à mort pour mutinerie et lâcheté devant l’ennemi

original_payload.original_title: RDC : 65 militaires condamnés à mort pour mutinerie et lâcheté devant l’ennemi
original_payload.original_body:
Un tribunal militaire de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a condamné à mort 65 militaires, reconnus coupables de mutinerie, de désobéissance aux ordres et de lâcheté devant l’ennemi. Selon des médias locaux, le verdict a été rendu à l’issue d’un procès tenu au tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma, dans la province du Nord-Kivu.
Au total, plus de 70 militaires ont comparu devant cette juridiction. Quatre prévenus ont été acquittés, tandis qu’un autre a été condamné à 10 ans de prison, rapporte Radio Okapi, la radio des Nations unies en RDC.
Les 66 militaires condamnés appartiennent au 3415e régiment de l’armée congolaise. Ils auraient été arrêtés le 20 octobre dernier dans le territoire de Walikale, où ils sont accusés d’avoir commis les faits qui leur sont reprochés.
Lire aussi :  RDC : l’Assemblée nationale adopte la loi sur le référendum dans un climat de tensions politiques
Cette décision intervient quelques semaines après une autre condamnation prononcée par une juridiction militaire congolaise. En octobre dernier, 27 soldats avaient également été condamnés à mort pour « lâcheté », après leur retrait des lignes de front lors des affrontements contre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23.
À travers ce procès, l’armée congolaise entend notamment renforcer la discipline au sein des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), dans un contexte marqué par la persistance de l’insécurité dans l’est du pays.
Ce nouveau verdict intervient alors que les combats se poursuivent dans l’est de la RDC entre les forces gouvernementales et la coalition rebelle Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), qui comprend notamment le mouvement M23. Les affrontements continuent d’alimenter la crise sécuritaire dans cette partie du pays.
