items.title: UNDP boosts community security in Terekeka County

original_payload.original_title: UNDP boosts community security in Terekeka County
original_payload.original_body:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), with support from the Peacebuilding Fund, is implementing community security activities in Terekeka County to strengthen trust between the police and the communities they serve and to reinforce grassroots peace structures.
Two Police-Community Relations Committees (PCRCs) have been established under the initiative. The committees were also provided with security kits and chairs to help them participate effectively in community security.
Mercyline Sikasa, the UNDP lead facilitator, said the support will equip the committees to contribute to safety in their areas through early warning and information sharing, as well as joint patrols with the police to prevent crime.
“We established two PCRCs and equipped them with security kits and chairs so that they can effectively take part in community security,” she said. “Through early warning, meaning information sharing, and joint patrols with the police, communities and police can work together to prevent crime before it happens.”
Sikasa added that the intervention is helping to close the gap between security providers and residents, while strengthening grassroots peace structures.
“When the community sees the police as partners and not as strangers, trust grows, and that is the foundation of lasting peace,” she said.
During the visit, the UNDP team paid a courtesy call on County Commissioner Abraham Kenyi John. The meeting was attended by the county’s executive director, Santo Abuli, the head of security, and other county leaders.
County officials expressed appreciation for UNDP’s support, including the renovation of the female wing of Terekeka prison.
“On behalf of the people of Terekeka County, I thank UNDP and its partners for the support they continue to give us,” Abuli said. “The renovation of the female wing of the prison and the work with the police and community show that you are committed to our people’s safety and dignity.”
Meanwhile, Salim Khamis Murasal, the Deputy Police Chief Inspector in Terekeka, also welcomed the initiative and said it would strengthen cooperation between officers and residents.
“The PCRCs will help us a lot. When citizens share information early and work with us on patrols, it becomes easier for the police to respond quickly and prevent crime,” he said. “This cooperation improves how the community sees the police, and how we serve the community.”
Community security is widely seen as a way to improve public safety through shared responsibility, with residents and police working together to identify and address local security concerns.

items.title: Communist Party condemns arrest of member in Damazin

original_payload.original_title: Communist Party condemns arrest of member in Damazin
original_payload.original_body:
The Sudanese Communist Party has condemned the detention of its resistance committee member in Damazin, the capital of Sudan’s Blue Nile region, and demanded that the authorities disclose his whereabouts and either release him or bring him before a court for a fair trial.
The arrest of Ahmed Babiker has drawn condemnation from political and human rights groups after he was detained by a security cell, with no official information available about the reasons for his arrest or his whereabouts.
A member of the Damazin Resistance Committee popularly known as “Jaghraf,” he was arrested by the security cell on Thursday, 5 November, while passing through the western entrance to the city on his way to work at a camp for internally displaced people.
Al-Tayyib Saad, a member of the Damazin Resistance Committees, told Radio Tamazuj that they are yet to receive information about Babiker’s place of detention or the reasons for his arrest. He said Babiker had not been allowed to contact his family or lawyer.
“The arrest is a violation of fundamental rights and international human rights standards,” he said. “We call on the security authorities to immediately disclose Babiker’s whereabouts, allow him access to his family and legal counsel, and guarantee his physical and psychological well-being.”
He reiterated the resistance committees’ opposition to what he called arbitrary arrests and enforced disappearances targeting the December Revolution youths and resistance committee members.
Saad stressed that Babiker should either be brought before a court for a fair trial if he faces criminal charges or be released immediately.
Meanwhile, the Sudanese Communist Party condemned the arrest, describing it as arbitrary.
“The party strongly condemns Babiker’s arrest by the security cell and demands that he either be brought before a court for a fair trial in accordance with the law or be released,” Mahjoub Al-Haj, a senior Communist Party official, told Radio Tamazuj.
Al-Haj said several other civilians had also been subjected to arbitrary arrests, expressing the party’s rejection of such practices and reiterating its condemnation of Babiker’s detention on behalf of the Communist Party in southern Blue Nile.
The arrest has also raised legal questions about the legitimacy of the security cell and the procedures it follows when detaining civilians.
Mohamed Nour Ali, a lawyer and human rights activist, told Radio Tamazuj that the security cell had emerged as a  de facto  body under wartime conditions but was, in his assessment, an unlawful entity established through a political decision.
He said that according to the information available to him, Babiker had been arrested without a warrant or any specific charges being brought against him.
He added that Babiker’s family had not been notified of his detention and that he had not been held in custody at any police station, but had instead been taken to an undisclosed location.
Ali said they were prepared to provide legal representation for Babiker should he be brought before the public prosecutor, noting that he had not yet been permitted to meet with a lawyer.
The arrest comes amid rapidly evolving security developments in Damazin, raising concerns about the potential impact of the security situation on civil liberties and political and civic activity across the region.
With no official information available about the circumstances of the arrest or Babiker’s place of detention, resistance committees and political groups continue to demand that the authorities disclose his whereabouts, safeguard his legal rights and personal safety, and clarify the legal grounds for his detention.

items.title: Cardinal Ameyu urges Sudan, South Sudan leaders to put citizens first

original_payload.original_title: Cardinal Ameyu urges Sudan, South Sudan leaders to put citizens first
original_payload.original_body:
Cardinal Stephen Ameyu Martin Mulla has urged political leaders in South Sudan and Sudan to prioritise the interests of citizens over political ambitions, saying compromise and dialogue are essential to addressing the challenges facing the two countries.
Speaking on Sunday at the opening of the 52nd Annual Plenary Assembly of the Sudan and South Sudan Catholic Bishops’ Conference in Torit, the cardinal said both countries face serious political, security and humanitarian challenges that require collective responsibility.
He identified the lack of political compromise as a major obstacle to resolving the crises, urging leaders to put the common good above personal and political interests.
“Compromise does not mean that you are a coward. It means that you give up your own position because of the common good,” Ameyu said.
He warned against continued reliance on armed conflict, saying it would only increase suffering among civilians.
“War cannot produce anything. It produces only death, hatred and destruction,” he said.
South Sudan elections
Ameyu also addressed South Sudan’s preparations for the December elections, urging voters to elect leaders capable of addressing their basic needs.
“Vote for your leaders who will bring to you all the necessary basic things in life,” he told the congregation.
He cautioned politicians against allowing electoral competition to result in violence, saying peaceful political engagement was in the interests of all citizens.
“No one will benefit from violence. Let us embrace the wisdom of God,” he said.
The cardinal also spoke about servant leadership, saying religious leaders had a responsibility to serve the people rather than dominate them.
Catholic bishops and Church representatives attend the opening of the 52nd Annual Plenary Assembly of the Sudan and South Sudan Catholic Bishops’ Conference in Torit, Eastern Equatoria State, on Sunday. (Photo: Radio Tamazuj)
Church calls for solidary
Ameyu expressed concern about the effects of drought on agricultural production and livelihoods in South Sudan, saying crop losses in several parts of the country had added to the difficulties facing vulnerable communities.
He urged Christians to maintain their faith and support one another during difficult times, emphasising the importance of collective responsibility.
“We will not be saved as individuals. We will be saved as a community of people living together in solidarity,” he said.
He called on communities to share available resources and avoid selfishness, saying solidarity and compassion were important in addressing the country’s challenges.
Meanwhile, Andrew Karlo Akwo, representing the Eastern Equatoria State Government, described the assembly as an important gathering for the Catholic Church in Sudan and South Sudan.
Akwo commended the Church for its contributions to education, healthcare, vocational training, social welfare, poverty alleviation and humanitarian assistance.
He said Church-run institutions, including schools, hospitals, clinics and rural dispensaries, complemented government efforts to provide essential services.
“We recognise the Church as the conscience of society,” Akwo said.
He described the government and the Church as partners in promoting peace, stability and human dignity.
“The government and the Church are mutual pillars supporting the stability of the nation,” he said.
Akwo urged the bishops to continue addressing national challenges and promoting reconciliation, unity and peaceful coexistence.
He also called for closer cooperation between the government and the Church in tackling poverty, economic recovery, climate change, environmental protection, migration and insecurity.
Bishops meet in Torit
The 52nd Annual Plenary Assembly brings together Catholic bishops from Sudan and South Sudan, clergy and representatives of Church institutions to discuss pastoral priorities, institutional matters and the Church’s role in peace and development.
The gathering comes as both countries face continuing political, security and humanitarian challenges.
The assembly provides a forum for Church leaders to discuss peace, reconciliation and their role in supporting communities in Sudan and South Sudan.

items.title: Palestine Weekly: West Bank on fire – and Gaza’s tents under water

original_payload.original_body:
The first major storm of the season flooded about 70,000 tents in Gaza within 12 hours, killing at least five people and causing about $3m in damage, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.
The storm hit over the weekend. By Monday, Gaza’s Civil Defence had logged more than 2,100 distress calls, warning that more than 2,000 buildings risk collapse. Nearly  400,000 displaced people shelter in areas  judged highly vulnerable.

Israel is blocking  60,000 mobile homes  and 200,000 tents, allowing only 20,000 tents into Gaza, where about 85 percent of homes have been destroyed or damaged by Israel’s three-year genocidal war.
Gaza’s Crossings and Borders Authority said Israel also let in no aid trucks or commercial goods on November 6 and 7; five trucks of cooking gas entered the next day. The UN’s Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) says Israel notified the UN on November 1 that it would suspend shipments from Egypt, and aid groups warn daily cooked meals could fall from about 600,000 to 330,000 as a result.
Gaza’s Ministry of Health says 20 more Palestinians were killed over the past week, bringing the toll since the October 2025 “ceasefire” to 1,613 as of November 9. Among them:
Storm collapse, November 8:  A sand embankment fell onto tents at a displacement site southwest of Deir el-Balah. Five bodies were recovered, among them Tahrir Nabhan and her daughter Maryam, and Habiba al-Zein.
Strikes and shootings:  On November 3, Rimas al-Madhoun, 16, was killed in a strike on a tent in Gaza City. Two days later, Noura Sheikh al-Eid was killed by tank fire in al-Mawasi hours after her daughter left for treatment in Egypt, and 12-year-old Adnan al-Qirnawi was shot and killed east of Bureij the same day. Nermin al-Amour and Mahmoud Abu Hammad were then killed on November 8 in a Khan Younis strike.

original_payload.original_body:
Luka Doncic has scored 32 points as the in-form Los Angeles Lakers have rolled to a sixth straight victory with a 124-114 defeat of the Atlanta Hawks in the NBA.
Doncic, whose  sensational early-season form  has propelled the Lakers to the top of the Western Conference, once again led from the front on Monday to secure an impressive win on the road.

The Slovenian star finished with 32 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds, five steals and two blocks in a dominant all-around performance.
Doncic, who is averaging 40 points per game this season, received offensive support from Sandro Mamukelashvili, who delivered an eye-catching 23 points from the bench, including five three-pointers.
Luka Doncic drives to the basket during the game against the Atlanta Hawks [Adam Hagy/Getty Images via AFP]   Walker Kessler added 21 points. Collin Sexton scored 18 and Ziaire Williams 12.

“Luka, again, just orchestrating. He was out there without a secondary ball handler, so he had to be on the ball a lot, and that was taxing. I thought he handled it well,” Redick added.

The attack in Sulaimaniyah governorate late on Sunday sparked a fire and forced the suspension of gas supplies to several power stations, initially reducing electricity generation in areas administered by the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) by between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts, according to regional officials.

KRG authorities have blamed Iran-backed groups in Iraq for  previous attacks  on the field in recent years.
The attack also comes days after the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK)  announced its withdrawal from the KRG , deepening a political crisis with its rival, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).

items.title: Can the Republican Party survive Trump?

original_payload.original_title: Can the Republican Party survive Trump?
original_payload.original_body:
There is a saying in politics: “Every election is fundamentally about the next one.” On November 3, the Republican Party suffered  what some have labelled a near “extinction-level” loss  in the 2026 midterms. With the results likely to offer an indication of what lies ahead in the next presidential election, what options do Republicans have for 2028? First, we need to understand why this latest “blue tsunami” occurred. The midterms were a rejection of Trump, not an endorsement of the Democrats.
Last Tuesday’s outcome reflected voters holding Trump responsible for economic disaster, huge increases in the cost of living, his failing war on Iran, and his catering to Israel. It is also a condemnation of the Trump family using the Oval Office to enrich themselves and their friends to an unprecedented degree.

original_payload.original_body:
The United Kingdom awarded 10.7 million pounds ($14.4m) in new public contracts to firms with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, despite British government pledges to punish companies that profit from settlement activity, an Al Jazeera investigation reveals.
The contracts were published after the British government announced new powers on September 8 to sanction companies profiting from business with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, which are illegal under international law.

An analysis of procurement records, company filings, corporate disclosures and contract data supplied by Tussell, a British public sector market intelligence firm, has found that businesses named by the United Nations over their involvement in illegal Israeli settlements – and companies that those businesses ultimately own or control as subsidiaries – have secured contracts across the British public sector.
The companies “appear to be in breach of their legal obligations under international humanitarian law”, Neve Gordon, a professor at the school of law at Queen Mary University of London, told Al Jazeera.
“Any UK company that is involved in the occupation is likely to be in direct breach of the sanctions regime Ed Miliband is putting in place,” Gordon said, referring to the UK foreign secretary.

European foreign ministers have told United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Europe must have a say in any deal to end Russia’s war on Ukraine, as US-mediated peace talks get under way in Abu Dhabi.
They made the appeal on Monday in Paris, at a meeting of foreign ministers from the Group of Seven, which includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States.

It was Rubio’s first meeting with allies since last week’s midterm elections, in which President Donald Trump’s Republican Party suffered stunning losses. The meeting gave Washington’s allies a chance to air their concerns with Rubio directly amid concern about Trump’s growing rhetoric of a new security architecture for Europe.
“It is certainly neither necessary, nor right, nor appropriate to make a fundamental change” to Europe’s security architecture, said German Minister for Foreign Affairs Johann Wadephul after talks with Rubio.
“Europe belongs at this table. There can be no solution without Europe – only with Europe,” he added.
The two-day Paris meeting, which ends on Tuesday, overlaps with the talks between Russia and Ukraine, scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday.
Wadephul said the Abu Dhabi talks must show whether Russia is “genuinely prepared to negotiate”, urging Moscow to “give up maximalist demands” and warning against any “negotiation show” in the capital of the United Arab Emirates.
With Russian attacks on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure continuing, he said, “we see no substantial contribution whatsoever toward negotiations gaining any serious momentum” from Moscow.

items.title: Moyen-Chari : deux ministères évaluent les investissements publics

original_payload.original_title: Moyen-Chari : deux ministères évaluent les investissements publics
original_payload.original_body:
Le ministère des Finances en collaboration avec le ministère de l’Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation, organise, du 9 au 12 novembre 2026, au Centre des jeunes Don Bosco de Sarh, un atelier consacré à l’examen des Programmes annuels d’investissement (PAI) 2026 de la province du Moyen-Chari. Cette initiative, appuyée par l’UNICEF, vise à apprécier les résultats des projets engagés, à identifier les insuffisances dans leur mise en œuvre et à définir des mesures pour améliorer les futurs investissements publics.
Pendant quatre jours, les participants analyseront les actions programmées, le niveau de réalisation des projets ainsi que les difficultés qui ont marqué leur exécution. Cet exercice doit également permettre de vérifier si les ressources mises à disposition ont été utilisées conformément aux objectifs prévus.
Au nom des deux ministères organisateurs, Solkam Béchir Sou 4 a expliqué que les PAI représentent un moyen important de transformer les orientations nationales en réalisations concrètes dans les provinces.

Elle a insisté sur la nécessité de ne pas se limiter à la programmation des activités, mais de s’intéresser également aux résultats obtenus sur le terrain. Elle a notamment appelé à renforcer les dispositifs de contrôle et d’évaluation afin de mieux suivre l’utilisation des ressources publiques, de repérer les retards et de trouver des réponses adaptées aux difficultés rencontrées.
Intervenant au nom du président du Conseil provincial du Moyen-Chari, le conseiller Ndanga Kel a, pour sa part, rappelé que la réussite des investissements doit se mesurer à travers leurs effets sur le quotidien des habitants. Il a estimé que les projets financés par les pouvoirs publics doivent apporter des réponses aux besoins prioritaires des communautés, notamment en matière de santé, d’éducation et d’accès aux services sociaux.
Le représentant du Conseil provincial a également encouragé une plus grande implication des populations dans le choix des projets et plaidé pour une utilisation rigoureuse et transparente des fonds publics. Il a souligné que les décisions prises en matière de développement doivent tenir compte des réalités vécues dans les différentes localités de la province.
Lire aussi :  « Sans investir dans les femmes, aucun PND ne peut réussir » Yewande Osarhieme Odiah
« Les conclusions attendues de cet atelier devront nous permettre de mieux orienter les prochaines programmations et de corriger les faiblesses relevées au cours de l’année 2026. Cette évaluation constitue pour nous une étape importante pour renforcer la gestion des ressources publiques et améliorer les résultats des actions de développement de notre province », a conclu le conseiller Ndanga Kel.

items.title: الرياضة في إفريقيا: تقرير دولي يكرس نموذج المناطق المتكاملة

original_payload.original_title: الرياضة في إفريقيا: تقرير دولي يكرس نموذج المناطق المتكاملة
original_payload.original_body:
SPORTS
الرياضة في إفريقيا: تقرير دولي يكرس نموذج المناطق المتكاملة
يسلط تقرير مشترك للبنك الدولي واللجنة الأولمبية والوكالة الفرنسية للتنمية الضوء على اقتصاد الرياضة بإفريقيا، داعياً إلى اعتماد نموذج المناطق الرياضية المتكاملة لضمان تنمية مستدامة.
Alwihda Info
10 nov. 2026
© Pixabay
يُسلط تقرير مرجعي، نُشر بشكل مشترك بين البنك الدولي، واللجنة الأولمبية الدولية (IOC)، والوكالة الفرنسية للتنمية (AFD)، الضوء على الإمكانات غير المستغلة لاقتصاد الرياضة في إفريقيا، داعياً إلى تطوير بنيات أساسية متكاملة. ويحمل التقرير عنوان "إطلاق العنان لإمكانات الرياضة في إفريقيا"، ويقع في 356 صفحة مستنداً إلى مسوحات أجريت في تسع دول ورسم تخطيطي للسياسات الرياضية لحوالي عشرين حكومة.
ويشير التقرير إلى أن اقتصاد الرياضة يمثل حالياً أقل من 1% من الناتج المحلي الإجمالي للقارة، مقابل حوالي 2,5% في أوروبا. ويُحذر من غياب البنيات الأساسية المتكاملة باعتباره أحد العوائق الرئيسية أمام هذا النمو، منبهاً إلى مخاطر ضعف استغلال الملاعب الكبرى المشيدة لفعاليات ظرفية، ومشيراً إلى أن عوائدها الاقتصادية المحلية غالباً ما تكون مؤقتة وغير مستدامة.
وفي مواجهة هذه الخلاصات، يوصي المؤلفون بدمج استراتيجيات الإرث منذ مرحلة التحضير، وربط الرياضة بقطاعات السياحة والنقل والخدمات، وتطوير الشراكات بين القطاعين العام والخاص، فضلاً عن هيكلة سلاسل القيمة المحلية.
وتتطابق هذه الاستنتاجات مع توجهات مجموعة التعاون الإفريقي (ACG)، وهي منصة متخصصة في تصنيع الرياضة بإفريقيا. ويهدف نموذجها القائم على "المناطق الرياضية والترفيهية" المختلطة إلى الجمع بين 15 إلى 20 نوعاً من الأصول (ملاعب، فنادق، محلات تجارية، أكاديميات) لتوليد مداخيل مستدامة.
وقال نيكولاس بومبينيه موغنار، المؤسس والرئيس التنفيذي لمجموعة (ACG): "لقد نشر البنك الدولي واللجنة الأولمبية الدولية والوكالة الفرنسية للتنمية للتو الأساس الواقعي لما تبنيه مجموعة (ACG) حالياً". وأضاف: "يؤكد التقرير أن الملاعب المعزولة، التي تُبنى من أجل بطولة وتُهمل بعد صافرة النهاية، لا تُحدث أثراً اقتصادياً مستداماً".
من جهته، يُعتقد المدير العام لمجموعة (ACG)، بابلو ج. كروز، أن هذا الإصدار يمنح مصادقة مؤسساتية لحاملي المشاريع، موضحاً: "لم يعد السؤال مطروحاً حول ما إذا كانت البنيات الأساسية الرياضية المتكاملة هي النموذج الصحيح لإفريقيا [...] بل السؤال هو من سيقوم ببنائها".
ومدعمومة بمجلس استشاري دولي وشخصيات بارزة من الحكامة الرياضية، تعتزم مجموعة (ACG) تمركز مشاريعها ضمن هذه التوجهات المؤسساتية الجديدة لتنمية القارة.
original_payload.original_summary: يسلط تقرير مشترك للبنك الدولي واللجنة الأولمبية والوكالة الفرنسية للتنمية الضوء على اقتصاد الرياضة بإفريقيا، داعياً إلى اعتماد نموذج المناطق الرياضية المتكاملة لضمان تنمية مستدامة.

N’Djamena : La Commune poursuit la lutte contre les moustiques dans trois arrondissements
admin
novembre 10, 2026
1 minutes de lecture
19 vues
La Commune de N’Djamena poursuit ses actions de prévention contre la dengue et le paludisme. Ce lundi 9 novembre 2026, les équipes de la Police municipale sont intervenues dans les 3e, 6e et 7e arrondissements pour identifier et éliminer les endroits favorables à la prolifération des moustiques.
L’opération a notamment porté sur le repérage et l’enlèvement des pneus usagés, qui peuvent retenir de l’eau et servir de lieux de reproduction aux moustiques responsables de la transmission de ces maladies.
À travers cette initiative, la municipalité entend réduire les risques sanitaires et renforcer la protection des populations contre la dengue et le paludisme.

original_payload.original_title:
Diplomatie 
             Niger-UE : le Premier ministre Ali Lamine Zeine reçoit le chargé d'affaires européen à Niamey

               Le Premier ministre Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine a reçu, lundi 9 novembre à Niamey, le chargé d'affaires de l'Union européenne au Niger, Olaï Voionmaa…

                     10 novembre 2026
original_payload.original_body:
Diplomatie
Niger-UE : le Premier ministre Ali Lamine Zeine reçoit le chargé d'affaires européen à Niamey
Le Premier ministre Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine a reçu, lundi 9 novembre à Niamey, le chargé d'affaires de l'Union européenne au Niger, Olaï Voionmaa. Aucune déclaration n'a filtré à la sortie de l'audience. L'entretien survient au lendemain des propos de Bruxelles sur le déploiement de soldats algériens, jugés inacceptables par Niamey.
Par  La Rédaction
·
10 novembre 2026 à 07h06
· 4 min de lecture
Le Premier ministre Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine recevant le chargé d'affaires de l'Union européenne au Niger, Olaï Voionmaa, le 9 novembre 2026 à Niamey. (Photo : ANP)
Le Premier ministre, ministre de l'Économie et des Finances, Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine, a reçu lundi 9 novembre à son cabinet de Niamey le chargé d'affaires de la Délégation de l'Union européenne au Niger, Olaï Voionmaa. Aucune déclaration n'a été faite à la presse à l'issue de cette audience, s'est bornée à noter l'Agence nigérienne de presse. Un silence qui pèse, au lendemain de propos européens que Niamey a qualifiés de « condescendants et inacceptables ».
L'entretien intervient dans un dossier brûlant. À la fin du mois d'octobre, Alger a annoncé le déploiement d'unités militaires au Niger pour protéger des intérêts énergétiques communs, une première depuis 1973. Bruxelles a réagi en demandant des « éclaircissements » sur la portée et l'objectif de cette initiative. La réponse de Niamey n'a pas traîné : les autorités ont rappelé qu'elles n'avaient « pas de permission à recevoir de Bruxelles » pour l'exercice de leur souveraineté, et exigé des clarifications sur ce qu'elles appellent des « ingérences répétées et désobligeantes ».
Des soldats algériens, une question de souveraineté
Le déploiement annoncé par Alger marque un tournant. C'est la première fois depuis 1973 que l'Algérie envoie des militaires hors de ses frontières. Le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune l'a justifié par la protection d'intérêts énergétiques partagés. Pour Niamey, ce partenariat bilatéral ne regarde pas l'Europe. Le gouvernement nigérien, qui place la souveraineté au cœur de sa politique étrangère depuis juillet 2023, n'entend pas se faire dicter ses alliances.
Cette posture s'inscrit dans une recomposition plus large. Depuis 2023, Niamey a diversifié ses partenaires, en direction de Moscou, de Pékin et d'Ankara, et a fondé avec le Mali et le Burkina Faso l'Alliance des États du Sahel. Dans ce nouvel alignement, la place de l'Europe ne va plus de soi : elle se négocie.
Du côté de la société civile, la méfiance envers Bruxelles reste vive. Rhamar Ilatoufegh, membre de la coordination de la société civile d'Arlit, dans le nord du pays, s'étonne que la Commission européenne s'intéresse tant au territoire nigérien. « Elle aurait pu demander à la France pourquoi elle a exploité 175 000 tonnes d'uranium en laissant les Nigériens parmi les populations les plus pauvres du monde », a-t-il lancé, cité par RFI. Pour lui, Bruxelles pratique le deux poids, deux mesures.
Une coopération européenne qui cherche à se réinventer
Depuis le coup d'État du 26 juillet 2023, la relation entre Niamey et Bruxelles est passée par toutes les tensions. L'Union européenne avait suspendu l'essentiel de sa coopération sécuritaire et de développement. Depuis, les deux parties tentent de reconstruire. En juin 2025, Olaï Voionmaa, qui assure l'intérim de la délégation, plaidait déjà pour « tourner la page et aller de l'avant ». En janvier 2026, l'envoyé spécial de l'UE pour le Sahel, João Cravinho, était venu présenter à Niamey une « approche renouvelée pour le Sahel », adoptée à Bruxelles fin 2025 et fondée, disait-il, sur l'engagement et le renforcement d'un dialogue respectueux.
L'UE reste un partenaire financier de poids. Elle finance des programmes de réintégration des migrants de retour et des projets agricoles comme AgrEcoNUS+, consacré aux semences et à la valorisation des ressources locales. Ces projets, eux, se poursuivent. C'est ce paradoxe que résume l'audience du 9 novembre : une coopération technique qui avance, une relation politique qui tangue.
Ce que Niamey attend : souveraineté d'abord, partenariat ensuite
Rien n'a filtré des discussions entre le Premier ministre et le chargé d'affaires européen. Le suivi des projets bilatéraux et la réorientation des axes de coopération figuraient à l'ordre du jour, selon les indications recueillies. Mais le message de fond est clair : le Niger entend choisir librement ses partenaires, qu'il s'agisse de l'Algérie, de ses alliés de l'Alliance des États du Sahel ou d'autres puissances.
La question reste entière : l'Union européenne saura-t-elle s'adresser à un Niger qui a fait de la souveraineté sa boussole, sans le traiter en vassal ? L'audience du 9 novembre n'a pas livré de réponse publique. Elle a au moins rouvert le canal, dans un climat où chaque mot compte.

original_payload.original_body:
Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba, has acknowledged being a political godfather but said he does not interfere in the administration of Governor Dapo Abiodun by imposing people on him for government appointments.
Osoba made the disclosure during an interview on The Reuben and Kike Abati Podcast, where he spoke with the media couple, Dr Reuben Abati and Kikelomo Atanda-Owo. A video of the conversation was shared on Sunday.
Responding to questions about godfatherism and calls for influential political figures to withdraw from politics, Osoba said he hardly interfered in Abiodun’s administration, despite offering him advice.
“And I can tell you one thing that is working for me in Ogun State is because I hardly interfere. Governor Dapo Abiodun, I counsel and advise him; I’ve never nominated one person into his government,” he said.

items.title: Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent to attract skilled workers

original_payload.original_title: Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent to attract skilled workers
original_payload.original_body:
Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme, creating a continuing pathway to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages.
The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia.
According to a release on Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) website, the programme will initially continue with the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to additional communities in the future.
The employer- and community-led initiative is designed to address the distinct workforce needs of rural Canada by connecting newcomers and their families with local employers and community support systems to encourage long-term settlement.

items.title: 2027: AGF, CJN warn judges against political pressure

original_payload.original_title: 2027: AGF, CJN warn judges against political pressure
original_payload.original_body:
The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), and the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, have warned judges appointed to serve on the 2027 Election Petition Tribunals against political interference, intimidation and other forms of external pressure.
They cautioned that compromised or erroneous electoral judgments could undermine public confidence in the judiciary and threaten Nigeria’s democratic stability.

“The true strength of the judiciary lies in its ability to uphold what is lawful and just, even when doing so is unpopular or inconvenient or may be misinterpreted.

items.title: NDIC laments debtors’ refusal to repay failed bank loans

original_payload.original_title: NDIC laments debtors’ refusal to repay failed bank loans
original_payload.original_body:
The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation has expressed concern over the refusal of some debtors of failed banks to repay outstanding loans, accusing them of deliberately frustrating recovery efforts through asset concealment, legal delays and intimidation.
The corporation warned that such practices undermine efforts to recover funds belonging to depositors and delay the payment of outstanding claims to customers of liquidated financial institutions.
The Director of the Asset Management Department of the NDIC, Ogungbemi Theophilus, raised the concerns on Monday during the Stakeholders’ Seminar and Public Relations Workshop held at Exclusive Serene Hotels and Suites, Wuye, Abuja.
Speaking on the challenges confronting the corporation in recovering assets of failed banks, Theophilus said, “Some debtors of failed banks believe that because a bank’s licence is revoked, he is not obliged to fulfil his responsibilities anymore. They hide assets. They frustrate service. Employ delay tactics in court. Sometimes, they try to intimidate. But we have to always do our job and professionally too.”

NGF, in a statement on Monday, signed by its Director-General, Abdullateef Shittu, explained that the initiative was designed to provide executive capacity development, applied research, governance advisory services, digital innovation and peer-learning opportunities for state-level political and administrative leaders.
It stated, “The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) has approved the establishment of the NGF Academy & Leadership Centre as a flagship Directorate within its secretariat, delivering executive capacity development, applied research, governance advisory services, digital innovation and structured peer learning within a unified, non-partisan institutional framework tailored to the governance realities of all 36 states.

original_payload.original_title: NELFUND won’t publish names of student loan beneficiaries – DG
original_payload.original_body:
The Nigerian Education Loan Fund has ruled out publishing the names of students benefiting from its loan scheme, citing data protection concerns and the need to protect beneficiaries from embarrassment and possible targeting.
The Director-General of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyerr, said the fund would only disclose the institutions that received payments and the number of beneficiaries, insisting that the identities of individual students would remain confidential.
Since the launch of the student loan portal on May 24, 2024, NELFUND has disbursed a total of  N375.28bn as of Monday, November 9, 2026, comprising N194.77bn in institutional fees and N180.50bn in upkeep allowances.
The fund also disclosed that 1,675,474 student loans had been disbursed across 320 beneficiary institutions.

Le match nul 2-2 entre le FC Twente et l’Ajax Amsterdam, dimanche 8 novembre à Enschede, s’est achevé sur une image inattendue. Tolu Arokodare et Wout Weghorst, adversaires et buteurs au cours de la rencontre, ont joint les mains avant de prier ensemble sur la pelouse.
L’attaquant nigérian Arokodare avait ouvert le score de la tête après un peu plus de deux minutes. Rayane Bounida a porté l’avance de l’Ajax à 2-0 à la 66e minute, avant qu’un but contre son camp de Dies Janse ne relance Twente deux minutes plus tard. Weghorst a égalisé sur penalty dans la cinquième minute du temps additionnel.
Après le coup de sifflet final, les deux attaquants se sont retrouvés au centre du terrain. Weghorst a expliqué à la chaîne publique néerlandaise NOS qu’ils se connaissaient bien et échangeaient régulièrement sur leur foi.
Leur relation remonte à un match amical entre Genk et Burnley, lorsque le Nigérian évoluait en Belgique et le Néerlandais en Angleterre. Selon Weghorst, Arokodare était venu lui demander des conseils après cette rencontre. Les deux joueurs sont restés en contact depuis.
Weghorst a ajouté qu’Arokodare lui avait proposé de prier après le match de dimanche. Les deux hommes, qui se disent croyants, ont alors rendu grâce avant de s’enlacer.
La séquence a réuni les deux principaux buteurs de la soirée. Arokodare a lancé l’Ajax dès la troisième minute, tandis que Weghorst, ancien joueur du club d’Amsterdam, a arraché le point du nul pour Twente à la 95e.

Les feux d’artifice tirés dimanche malgré les restrictions de la justice ont ajouté des particules à la pollution qui frappe déjà la capitale indienne.
Environnement      Par  Eudoxie Nguessan
·   10 Nov. 2026 à 08:24  10/11/26 08:24       ·   2 min  de lecture

Nuage de pollution au-dessus de Delhi vu par le satellite NOAA-20 le 31 octobre 2019 (archives). Photo : NOAA / domaine public.
Partager

Delhi s’est réveillée sous une épaisse couche de smog lundi 9 novembre 2026, au lendemain des célébrations de Diwali. À 9 heures, l’indice de qualité de l’air (AQI) de la capitale indienne atteignait 370, un niveau classé « très mauvais » par l’organisme national de contrôle de la pollution. Dans plusieurs quartiers, les relevés dépassaient 400, seuil de la catégorie « sévère ».
La brume grisâtre réduisait la visibilité autour de la Porte de l’Inde, ou India Gate, monument situé au centre de New Delhi. Des habitants ont signalé des irritations des yeux et de la gorge. La dégradation a suivi une nuit de festivités marquée par des tirs de pétards jusque tard dans la soirée, également signalés à Mumbai.
La Cour suprême avait limité l’utilisation des feux d’artifice aux modèles certifiés à émissions réduites, dans des créneaux horaires précis pendant le week-end de Diwali. Ces pétards dégagent eux aussi des particules polluantes. Leur fumée s’est ajoutée aux émissions des véhicules, des activités industrielles et des chantiers.
Chaque automne, les brûlages de résidus agricoles dans les États voisins du Pendjab et de l’Haryana contribuent également à charger l’air du nord de l’Inde. Avec la baisse des températures et les vents faibles, les polluants se dispersent moins facilement au-dessus de la métropole.
La qualité de l’air était déjà très dégradée avant la fête. Mercredi 4 novembre, l’indice avait atteint 377, tandis que les autorités renforçaient le nettoyage des routes, les mesures contre les déplacements automobiles et les services de transport public pour limiter les émissions.
Depuis vendredi, d’autres restrictions visent notamment certains travaux de construction et les groupes électrogènes fonctionnant au diesel. Les établissements scolaires ont aussi été invités à assurer des cours en ligne afin de réduire l’exposition des élèves lors des épisodes de pollution.

M. John Harrison a remporté lundi 9 novembre à Londres le Booker Prize 2026 pour  The End of Everything . À 81 ans, l’écrivain britannique devient le plus âgé des lauréats de ce prix littéraire, assorti de 50 000 livres sterling.
Son treizième roman suit un homme et sa tante sur la côte du Kent, dans une société britannique bouleversée par une catastrophe inexpliquée et l’apparition d’êtres extraterrestres. Le récit laisse volontairement une partie de ces événements dans l’ombre, plaçant le lecteur face à la même désorientation que les personnages.
Le jury présidé par Mary Beard a choisi ce livre à l’unanimité après une journée de délibérations. Il avait examiné 163 ouvrages pour cette édition. Le prix était ouvert aux auteurs de toute nationalité, pour un roman écrit en anglais et publié au Royaume-Uni ou en Irlande entre le 1er octobre 2025 et le 30 septembre 2026.
Cette distinction couronne une carrière commencée dans les années 1960, au cours de laquelle Harrison a notamment exploré la science-fiction et le fantastique. Il succède à David Szalay, récompensé en 2025. Parmi les cinq autres finalistes figuraient deux anciens lauréats, Marlon James, primé en 2015, et Douglas Stuart, vainqueur en 2020.

Deux personnes ont été arrêtées lundi 9 novembre 2026 aux abords de la Maison-Blanche, à Washington, après deux incidents survenus presque simultanément près du parc Lafayette. La résidence présidentielle a été brièvement bouclée alors que Donald Trump s’y trouvait, a indiqué le Secret Service américain.
Peu avant 10 heures, heure locale, une voiture est montée sur le trottoir au carrefour de la 16e rue et de H Street, au nord du parc. Son conducteur s’est opposé aux agents intervenus sur place, avant d’être interpellé par les équipes du Secret Service et de la Garde nationale.
Au même moment, une seconde personne a franchi une barrière de sécurité à l’angle nord-ouest de Lafayette Park. Elle a également été arrêtée rapidement, selon le service fédéral chargé de protéger le président des États-Unis.
La police a fermé temporairement plusieurs rues autour du parc. Une équipe spécialisée dans les explosifs a été appelée pour inspecter la voiture à titre préventif, pendant que les forces de sécurité contrôlaient les accès aux abords de la Maison-Blanche.
Des journalistes présents dans l’enceinte présidentielle ont été dirigés vers une salle du bâtiment pendant l’intervention. La restriction des déplacements a ensuite été levée dans la matinée.
Le Secret Service a ouvert des enquêtes sur les deux interpellations. Les autorités n’ont pas communiqué les motifs des personnes arrêtées ni établi si les deux événements étaient liés.

L’Ouganda sera privé de Rogers Mato contre le Botswana, samedi 14 novembre, dans les éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations 2027. Le sélectionneur Paul Put a confirmé le forfait de l’attaquant de Heart of Midlothian, touché lors d’un match de championnat d’Écosse face aux Rangers.
Mato avait quitté la pelouse à la 32e minute du nul (2-2) entre Hearts et les Rangers, après avoir ressenti des douleurs au mollet et au tendon d’Achille. Son état laissait encore espérer une participation au rassemblement. « Mato ne jouera pas », a finalement indiqué Paul Put dans des déclarations rapportées mardi 10 novembre par le média ougandais Kawowo Sports.
La préparation des Cranes a commencé lundi 9 novembre avec seulement neuf joueurs à l’entraînement, selon le technicien belge. La Fédération ougandaise de football (FUFA) a confirmé la tenue de cette première séance au Mandela National Stadium. Les internationaux évoluant à l’étranger doivent rejoindre progressivement le groupe. Paul Put espère disposer de son effectif au complet mercredi 11 novembre.

Le sélectionneur attend également un feu vert de la FIFA concernant Abdoulaye Sissako. La participation de David Udoh Akpan demeure incertaine. À ce stade, Paul Put n’a signalé aucun autre forfait pour blessure que celui de Rogers Mato.

L’excédent commercial de la Chine a atteint 1 040 milliards de dollars entre janvier et octobre 2026, selon les chiffres des douanes publiés mardi 10 novembre. Le pays franchit ainsi le seuil des 1 000 milliards un mois plus tôt qu’en 2025.
En octobre, les exportations ont progressé de 35,2 % sur un an, à 412,3 milliards de dollars. Les importations ont augmenté de 41,6 %, à 307,1 milliards. Ces montants concernent le seul mois d’octobre, tandis que l’excédent de 1 040 milliards correspond au cumul des dix premiers mois.
La demande mondiale de produits liés à l’intelligence artificielle, notamment les puces, les serveurs et les équipements de réseau, contribue à la poussée des exportations. Celles-ci soutiennent une économie freinée par les difficultés de l’immobilier et la faiblesse de la consommation intérieure.
Le déséquilibre se creuse aussi avec l’Union européenne. L’excédent chinois envers les Vingt-Sept atteint 310,7 milliards de dollars sur les dix premiers mois, contre 241,6 milliards sur la même période de 2025.
Sur l’ensemble de 2025, la Chine avait enregistré un excédent record de 1 200 milliards de dollars.

Les précommandes de « Grand Theft Auto VI » dépassent largement les prévisions initiales de Take-Two Interactive, a affirmé lundi 9 novembre 2026 son PDG Strauss Zelnick. L’éditeur maintient la sortie du jeu au 19 novembre sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X et S, treize ans après « GTA V ».
En présentant les résultats financiers trimestriels du groupe, Strauss Zelnick a décrit une demande « sans précédent ». Take-Two n’a pas publié de nombre officiel de précommandes, mais a confirmé que les réservations avaient largement dépassé ses attentes de départ.

Au trimestre achevé le 30 septembre, les réservations nettes du groupe ont atteint 1,60 milliard de dollars, soit 18 % de moins qu’un an plus tôt. Son chiffre d’affaires comptable s’est établi à 1,50 milliard de dollars sur la même période.
Le calendrier présenté le 9 novembre confirme une commercialisation sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X et S dès le 19 novembre. Aucune version pour ordinateur ne figure dans cette annonce de lancement.

English (World)
Qantas prévoit de confier à Accenture 850 emplois de ses fonctions administratives en Australie, dont la majorité sera transférée en Inde. Dans un courriel interne au personnel rapporté par la BBC, la directrice générale Vanessa Hudson annonce mardi 10 novembre un démarrage des changements à partir de mi-2027.
Les services financiers, les achats, les ressources humaines et le marketing seront les premiers concernés. Une partie du travail restera assurée en Australie. La compagnie indique qu’elle cherchera à reclasser les salariés touchés lorsque cela sera possible.
Ce partenariat pluriannuel doit accompagner la modernisation informatique de Qantas. Vanessa Hudson explique que la compagnie utilise plus de 1 000 applications anciennes qui n’ont pas été conçues pour fonctionner ensemble. L’entreprise prévoit ensuite de recourir davantage à l’automatisation et à l’intelligence artificielle pour les activités confiées à Accenture.
Qantas emploie environ 28 000 personnes en Australie et 4 000 ailleurs dans le monde. La direction dit discuter du projet avec les salariés et les syndicats.

items.title: Bayern Munich : Uli Hoeneß doute que Jamal Musiala retrouve son meilleur niveau

Bayern Munich : Uli Hoeneß doute que Jamal Musiala retrouve son meilleur niveau
Le président d’honneur du Bayern Munich a évoqué le suivi neurologique du joueur de 23 ans et dit ignorer s’il retrouvera son rendement antérieur. Le club annonce parallèlement son retour dans le groupe à l’entraînement.
Football      Par  André Kouagou Assane
·   10 Nov. 2026 à 06:16  10/11/26 06:16       ·   2 min  de lecture

Écouter

Uli Hoeneß a exprimé dimanche ses doutes sur la capacité de Jamal Musiala à retrouver le niveau qui était le sien avant ses problèmes de santé. Le président d’honneur du Bayern Munich s’est montré prudent alors que le milieu offensif allemand poursuit son retour progressif.
Invité de l’émission « Sonntags-Stammtisch » de la télévision régionale BR, l’ancien président du club a parlé d’un « dilemme ». Il a estimé que le suivi médical permettait de contrôler le trouble neurologique du joueur, sans pouvoir assurer que celui-ci retrouverait toutes ses capacités sportives.
Ses propos concernent les crises d’absence évoquées par Jamal Musiala cette année. Le joueur avait expliqué être suivi par des spécialistes pour un dysfonctionnement neurologique temporaire, qu’il présentait comme bien traitable et sans risque supplémentaire pour sa santé.
Cette situation médicale est distincte de la blessure musculaire qui a retardé son retour en compétition. Le Bayern a récemment annoncé que Musiala avait repris l’entraînement collectif après une lésion aux ischio-jambiers, tout en précisant qu’il n’était pas encore disponible pour les matches.
Le joueur de 23 ans avait déjà été ménagé à plusieurs reprises depuis le début de la saison. Son absence a privé l’équipe d’un de ses principaux créateurs dans les trente derniers mètres, mais le staff bavarois a jusqu’ici refusé de fixer un calendrier précis.
Le Bayern continue donc d’avancer par étapes dans sa reprise. Le club n’a communiqué aucune date de retour en compétition.

Le président camerounais Paul Biya a convoqué les électeurs aux urnes pour le dimanche 7 février 2027. Le décret signé lundi 9 novembre fixe à cette date les élections des députés à l’Assemblée nationale et des conseillers municipaux.
Ces deux scrutins ont été reportés à deux reprises. Les députés et conseillers municipaux actuellement en fonction avaient été élus en février 2020 pour un mandat de cinq ans, prolongé depuis.
Pour les élus municipaux, la dernière prorogation a été décidée par un décret du 4 mai 2026. Leur mandat court jusqu’au 28 février 2027, soit trois semaines après le vote désormais annoncé.
Dans un décret distinct, Paul Biya a également renouvelé pour quatre ans le mandat des douze membres du Conseil électoral d’Elections Cameroon, l’organisme chargé de l’organisation des élections. Enow Abrams Egbe en reste le président.

Deux changements pour les Panthères. Après le malaise du gardien Junior François Bekalé et le forfait de l’attaquant Orphé Mbina, le Gabon a appelé Joël Mboré et Alan Do Marcolino.

Partager
Ajouter Bénin Web TV à vos sources préférées
SOMMAIRE
Orphé Mbina remplacé en attaque
Le Gabon a procédé lundi 9 novembre à deux changements dans sa sélection pour la double confrontation contre le Lesotho, prévue les 13 et 17 novembre dans les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Le gardien Joël Mboré et l’attaquant Alan Do Marcolino remplacent respectivement Junior François Bekalé et Orphé Mbina, a annoncé la Fédération gabonaise de football.
Junior François Bekalé a été victime dimanche 8 novembre d’un malaise accompagné d’une crise convulsive à bord d’un avion transportant une partie des Panthères de Libreville vers Franceville. Il a bénéficié d’une prise en charge immédiate par le personnel médical de la sélection présent à bord. La Fédération a annoncé des examens complémentaires pour établir son état de santé.
Dans l’attente de ce bilan, le sélectionneur Sébastien Migné a décidé de laisser le gardien au repos et de convoquer Joël Mboré, qui évolue à Mangasport. Le portier découvre la sélection nationale A. La Fédération n’a communiqué aucun diagnostic sur la cause du malaise de Bekalé.
Orphé Mbina remplacé en attaque
Le deuxième changement concerne Orphé Mbina, attaquant du Sabah FK en Azerbaïdjan. Le joueur présente une gêne récurrente à l’adducteur gauche. Son club a demandé une semaine de repos, accordée par le staff médical des Panthères, ce qui entraîne son forfait pour le rassemblement de novembre.
Pour compléter le secteur offensif, Sébastien Migné a rappelé Alan Do Marcolino, qui joue au FK Ústí nad Labem, en deuxième division tchèque. L’attaquant rejoint le groupe chargé de préparer les deux rencontres face au Lesotho.
Le Gabon recevra le Lesotho vendredi 13 novembre à Franceville, avant de jouer la seconde manche mardi 17 novembre en Afrique du Sud. Les Panthères occupent la deuxième place du groupe A avec trois points après deux journées, derrière le Maroc, qui en compte six. Le Lesotho est quatrième, sans point.

items.title: COP31: Mozambique seeks increased climate finance for vulnerable countries

original_payload.original_title: COP31: Mozambique seeks increased climate finance for vulnerable countries
original_payload.original_body:
Photo: AIM The Mozambican Presidency announced yesterday that the Head of State will attend COP31 with the aim of mobilising international cooperation to address the impacts of climate change and increase funding for the most vulnerable countries,
In a statement, the Presidency said that Daniel Chapo would take part in several high-level meetings and events held as part of the COP31 conference, dedicated to discussing global challenges and responses to climate change.
“Mozambique’s participation in this summit aims to reaffirm the country’s national commitment to global climate action and mobilise international cooperation to address the impacts of climate change, with particular attention to the need to strengthen climate finance for the most vulnerable countries,” the statement reads.
READ:  Mozambique: President Chapo heads to Antalya for COP31 climate summit
The World Climate Action Summit, which forms part of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), is taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, until 20 November. The Mozambican President is scheduled to attend on 11 and 12 November.
According to the Presidency, the Head of State will be accompanied by the First Lady, Gueta Chapo; the Minister in the Presidency for Civil Affairs, Ricardo Sengo; the Secretary of State for Land and Environment, Gustavo Dgedge; as well as officials from the Office of the President and other State institutions.
The summit is being held under the theme “Towards a Sustainable, Resilient and Equitable Future” and brings together more than 100 countries belonging to the European Union and the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS), representing around two billion people and more than half of the members of the United Nations.
The main areas of cooperation include climate adaptation and resilience, access to climate finance, clean electrification and a just energy transition, as well as science, technology, climate capacity-building, food systems, water, resilient ecosystems and international ocean governance.
On the financial front, participants aim to mobilise at least US$300 billion (€262 billion) annually for climate action by 2035.
In the energy sector, the objective is to accelerate clean electrification and access to energy through investment in renewable energy, electricity grids and storage systems, within the framework of a transition described as “just, orderly and equitable” towards reducing dependence on fossil fuels.
The Presidency also recalls that the European Union and the OACPS signed the Samoa Agreement in November 2023, establishing the partnership framework between the two organisations for the next 20 years.
Provisionally applied since January 2024, the agreement covers areas including sustainable development, economic growth, human rights, peace and security, as well as strengthening cooperation in international forums.
Source:  Lusa

items.title: Mozambique: Maputo Central Hospital introduces first endoscopic technique of its kind in the country

original_payload.original_title: Mozambique: Maputo Central Hospital introduces first endoscopic technique of its kind in the country
original_payload.original_body:
FILE – For illustration purposes only. [File photo: Lusa] Maputo Central Hospital (HCM), Mozambique’s largest healthcare facility, has introduced the country’s first endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) technique. It is the only centre in the country currently offering the procedure to treat diseases affecting the pancreas and bile ducts, it was announced on Friday.
The technique makes it possible to treat certain obstructions of the bile and pancreatic ducts without resorting to conventional surgery. It involves inserting a flexible tube through the digestive tract, explained HCM Clinical Director Dércio Fernandes, speaking to journalists.
“In the past, when a patient had stones in the bile ducts, it was necessary to open the abdomen and make an incision in the duct to remove them. With this procedure, there is no longer any need to open up the patient’s abdomen, because we can reach the site through endoscopy and remove the stones,” Dércio Fernandes said.
He described the introduction of the procedure as a technological advance for the hospital, stressing that the technique makes it possible to treat patients with bile duct stones and certain pancreatic conditions through a less invasive intervention.
“We are here to celebrate the introduction of a new technique at our hospital. It is a technological advance and, as far as we know, we are the first centre in the country to offer this procedure,” Dércio Fernandes said.
According to HCM gastroenterologist Luzmira Mutambe, 12 procedures were performed during the first week of implementation, half of which were related to pancreatic conditions and the remainder to bile duct stones.
ERCP is performed by inserting a flexible tube through the mouth, passing it through the oesophagus and stomach into the duodenum. This allows doctors to access the bile and pancreatic ducts to identify and treat certain obstructions, avoiding the need for conventional surgery in some cases.
Source:  Lusa

items.title: Tunisian boatbuilders find a niche in global luxury yacht market

original_payload.original_title: Tunisian boatbuilders find a niche in global luxury yacht market
original_payload.original_body:
A boat built by Rassas Composites speeds across the water during sea trials off Bizerte, Tunisia. November 3, 2026. [Photo: Reuters/Jihed Abidellaoui]
Tunisia’s exports of yachts and pleasure boats reached €500 million last year – trade association
Some 75 companies operate in sector, up from about 20 a decade ago
Industry aims to double exports by 2030
Amid the hum of electric ​routers, Tarek Rassas watches craftsmen put the finishing touches to a luxury catamaran destined to sail from ‌Tunisia soon to a wealthy buyer abroad.
Rassas’ boatyard in the northern port city of Bizerte is part of a fast-growing yacht building and pleasure boat industry in Tunisia, which is trying to leverage its skilled workforce, competitive costs and proximity to Europe to take advantage of rising ​global demand for luxury vessels.
While few may be able to afford the yachts in Tunisia itself, where average wages ​are just a few hundred dollars a month, exports have grown rapidly over the past decade ⁠to around €500 million ($558.00 million) last year, the North African country’s trade association says.
Rassas says his business, founded by his father ​three decades ago to build small pleasure boats, now produces 10 yachts a year, catamarans and smaller yachts, which sell for ​up to €400,000 each. He employs around 60 people.
“It is always very satisfying to see these models being launched into the water, after a great deal of work having been done beforehand,” Rassas said. “It’s like watching your child set sail.”
Award-winning catamaran
Tunisia’s yacht building sector as a whole has ​grown to about 75 companies, from around 20 a decade ago, Montassar Dhiaf, head of Tunisia’s Marine Industries Association, the trade ​association, told Reuters.
Many of these are now Tunisian-owned and operated, unlike previously when foreign firms were more dominant, he said.
One sign of the ‌industry’s ⁠progress is that a luxury catamaran, the WAMA 42XL, built by a Tunisian company, won the under-45-foot power category in the 2026 Multihull of the Year awards, which recognise the best new multihull yachts and catamarans internationally.
Dhiaf says foreign expertise, particularly from Italian firms, helped transfer technology and develop local skills, enabling Tunisian companies to move from making components to building and exporting ​complete yachts.
“Tunisian companies can now ​handle the entire process, from ⁠design and manufacturing to outfitting and after-sales services,” Dhiaf said.
Yacht makers in Menzel Jemil near Bizerte also provided some of the components for Portuguese football star Cristiano Ronaldo’s luxury superyacht, he ​said.
French yacht makers, including the Beneteau Group, operate in Tunisia as well, and the sector ​aims to double ⁠its exports by 2030, which could boost foreign currency reserves and create jobs, Dhiaf said.
He called on the government to provide support, establish training centres and offer tax incentives to make Tunisian companies even more competitive.
Rassas said his own business – currently spread across five ⁠boatyards – aims ​to double output and expand production of luxury catamarans, which can take ​two months or more to build.
Models range in length from 7 to 25 metres (23-82 ft), Rassas said. One 11-metre model currently being built will feature three ​cabins and reach speeds of 25 knots, he added.
Source:  Reuters

items.title: ANC to review coalition ties after voting setback

original_payload.original_title: ANC to review coalition ties after voting setback
original_payload.original_body:
Image: Bloomberg South Africa’s biggest political party will consider whether to end its national coalition with its main rival after suffering its worst electoral performance yet—an argument that’s emerging as a fault line in the race to succeed President Cyril Ramaphosa.
Some members of the African National Congress’ (ANC) national executive committee are discussing how to make the case at a meeting on Thursday.
They will argue that the party’s tie-up with the Democratic Alliance in 2024 cost it votes in last week’s municipal elections, and that it should end, according to people familiar with the matter.
A previous push within the ANC to jettison the DA failed, and it’s unclear how much support the proposal would have this time around, they said.
But a reconfiguration of the so-called government of national unity, which has sought to prioritise growing the economy and creating jobs, could rattle investors, with the DA seen as a driver behind attempts to push through more business-friendly policies.
The ANC won just shy of 31% support in the 4 November vote and failed to win outright control of any of the eight biggest cities, while the DA increased its backing to almost 25%, retained its majority in Cape Town and got the most votes in several other metropolises.
Aggrieved ANC members plan to stake out who the party should partner with ahead of its December 2027 elective conference, when Ramaphosa is due to step down as its leader, the people said.
Deputy President Paul Mashatile and ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula are among those in contention to succeed him, while some party officials are promoting billionaire businessman Patrice Motsepe as a potential candidate.
Ramaphosa raised the possibility of stepping down as ANC leader in a discussion with the party’s top officials after the election, the Sunday Times reported.
Other officials pushed back, and one proposed bringing the elective conference forward to April, the Johannesburg-based newspaper said.
The president told reporters there was no truth to rumours that he would vacate his post early.
Some officials want ActionSA to take the DA’s place in the country’s 10-member GNU, the people said.
Led by former Johannesburg Mayor Herman Mashaba, ActionSA has six lawmakers and would give a reconfigured coalition 206 seats in the 400-member National Assembly if all the other partners stayed.
It’s unclear whether ActionSA would agree to a national deal.
The municipal vote was the ANC’s third major electoral setback under Ramaphosa. It won about 40% support nationally in 2024, losing its parliamentary majority for the first time since it took power after apartheid ended three decades earlier.
Relations between the ANC and the DA have been fractious since they teamed up, with the two parties clashing over the 2025 budget and several pieces of legislation.
Mbalula last month called for a review of the DA’s role in the coalition after it opposed the ANC’s court bid to reinstate its candidates who had been excluded from standing in the municipal elections on procedural grounds.
ANC officials critical of the partnership argue that the improvement in market confidence has yet to translate into stronger investment.
Fixed investment fell to 13.9% of gross domestic product in 2025, according to the central bank.
The NEC meeting will give direction on how the ANC will approach coalition talks in councils that no party won outright, including Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Tshwane in the central Gauteng province.
The ANC could partner with the DA, seek deals with other parties or go into opposition, the people said.
ActionSA representatives met Mbalula and other ANC officials on Sunday to discuss its conditions for entering into coalitions.
Several parties are exploring deals that would sideline the DA and complicate a bid by its former leader Helen Zille to become Johannesburg mayor.
The DA’s federal executive council said it had resolved to engage all political parties in discussions about forming coalitions in hung municipalities, with the objective of establishing stable, effective governments that put citizens first.
Mbalula told reporters the ANC will announce its position on coalitions on 13 November, and won’t comment until then.
The new metro councils must convene within 14 days of being declared elected.
Source:  Bloomberg

items.title: Botswana to double De Beers holding under Anglo stake sale, president says

original_payload.original_title: Botswana to double De Beers holding under Anglo stake sale, president says
original_payload.original_body:
FILE – A De Beers Group sign is displayed on the exterior of the diamond producer's headquarters in Gaborone, Botswana, October 19, 2026. [File photo: Reuters/Stringer]
Botswana currently holds a 15% stake in De Beers
Botswana aims to become largest shareholder in diamond producer
De Beers put up for sale amid falling diamond prices
Botswana will double its holding in De Beers to 30% under the ​terms of Anglo American’s proposed sale of its stake in the diamond producer to a consortium of investors, the country’s president said ‌on Monday, confirming support for the deal.
Botswana’s backing is key for the sale to progress, as the country has the right of first refusal on Anglo American’s stake. Under the terms of the deal it would become De Beers’ single largest shareholder, President Duma Boko said.
Anglo American put De Beers up for sale in 2024 as part of a wider restructuring amid falling diamond ​prices and growing demand for synthetic stones. A Botswanan government official said in July the miner had chosen the Global Diamond Consortium as preferred bidder.
President ​Boko said on Monday that Botswana supported the sale to the consortium, which is being led by former De Beers CEO ⁠Gareth Penny.
“This means that, when this transaction is complete, Botswana’s shareholding in De Beers will double from the current 15% to 30%,” Boko said in a ​speech in parliament.
“Botswana will become the single largest shareholder in De Beers, and with that comes greater influence in the strategic decisions for decades to come.”
Boko said the ​governments of Namibia and Angola would participate in the De Beers transaction.
‘A new chapter’
Swiss luxury group Richemont, owner of Cartier, is among companies in talks to join the Global Diamond Consortium.
Two people — a De Beers sightholder, or rough diamond buyer, and a diamond industry insider — told Reuters that sightholders Diarough, Pluczenik and Grandview Klein Diamonds, as well as jewellery maker Signet, are also ​part of the talks.
Indian company Rosy Blue India, which had previously been involved, has now withdrawn interest, one person said.
“De Beers once taught the world to desire ​diamonds. Its prospective owners now face the immense task of rekindling that desire at a time when luxury fashion houses and watchmakers have completely stolen the consumer spotlight,” said Tobias ‌Kormind, managing ⁠director of jewellery brand 77 Diamonds.
“Bringing together heavyweights like Signet, Richemont, and major sightholders like Pluczenik and Diarough means key players across the supply chain are uniting to back a natural diamond recovery.”
Anglo American said on Monday it would continue to work with Botswana, other governments and the Global Diamond Consortium towards agreeing binding transaction documents.
Penny said the consortium was working with the governments of Botswana, Angola, Namibia and Oman towards becoming co-owners of De Beers, and was focused on finalising agreements with ​Anglo as soon as possible.
“Together, we ​believe we can create a new ⁠chapter for this iconic business, one defined by strategic clarity between producing countries and the wider value chain, stronger consumer connection, and sustained growth in demand for natural diamonds,” Penny said in a statement.
Moving beyond the traditional diamond market
Botswana’s stake in ​De Beers gives it exposure not only to natural diamonds but also to advanced technology through Element Six, the miner’s ​synthetic diamond business, Boko ⁠said.
“Our investment in De Beers is not just an investment in natural diamonds. It is an investment in technology,” he said.
Boko said that Element Six will participate in a planned $600 million synthetic diamond plant that Reuters reported in January will be built in the US.
Demand for synthetic diamonds used in high-performance computing is likely to rise as artificial ⁠intelligence and large-scale ​data centres expand, the president added.
The US government had asked Element Six to partner on synthetic ​diamond technology, Boko said.
He said he had agreed with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick that the company should form the core of a new technology partnership between Botswana and the United States.
Source:  Reuters

items.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking

original_payload.original_title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
original_payload.original_body:
FILE – Fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France were affected last month. [File photo: AFP] France has accused Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month.
Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was “unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression”, adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions.
Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.
The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked.
Barrot said the attack on France’s supermarkets “marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation’s interests and the security of the French people”.
He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to “lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act”.
France will take “any other necessary and proportionate measures” to respond to the incident and “deter anyone who might seek to repeat it”, Barrot added.
The Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies.
Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC.
Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime.
In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year.
If the IRGC carried out the cyber-attacks, it remains unclear whether they were part of Iran’s deterrence strategy.
On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France’s supermarkets.
More than 100 of Coopérative U’s supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.
Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.
The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.
Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe.
Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.
Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects.
In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them.
The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations.
Source:  BBC

items.title: África do Sul detém nove suspeitos de recrutamento militar para a Rússia

original_payload.original_title: África do Sul detém nove suspeitos de recrutamento militar para a Rússia
original_payload.original_body:
Nove estrangeiros foram detidos na África do Sul, suspeitos de tentarem viajar para a Rússia com o objectivo de combater na guerra contra a Ucrânia. As detenções ocorreram no Aeroporto Internacional O.R. Tambo e num hotel próximo, em Joanesburgo, na sequência de uma investigação que envolveu os serviços de informações, a Interpol e forças de segurança locais e internacionais.
Segundo a polícia sul-africana, os suspeitos, com idades entre os 20 e os 26 anos, foram detidos na noite de domingo, quando se preparavam para embarcar em voos com destino à Rússia.
De acordo com o coronel Katlego Mogale, a operação foi desencadeada com base em informações recolhidas pelos serviços de informações. As autoridades não revelaram as nacionalidades dos detidos nem a que lado do conflito pretendiam alegadamente juntar-se.
Os nove suspeitos deverão responder perante o Tribunal de Magistrados de Kempton Park por crimes relacionados com alegadas violações da Lei de Regulamentação da Assistência Militar Estrangeira, que proíbe actividades mercenárias e regula a participação de cidadãos e estrangeiros em conflitos militares fora do país.
As detenções ocorrem num contexto de crescente preocupação com o recrutamento de cidadãos africanos para combater pela Rússia, em alguns casos através de promessas de emprego civil, formação e benefícios financeiros.
Uma investigação da organização Code for Africa, citada pelo Instituto de Estudos de Segurança, identificou 289 plataformas digitais, entre páginas, domínios e perfis nas redes sociais, utilizados para atrair potenciais recrutas através de anúncios enganosos e promessas de benefícios generosos.
A África do Sul já esteve envolvida em processos de repatriamento de cidadãos que terão sido atraídos para o conflito. Entre os casos investigados está o de Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla, filha do antigo Presidente Jacob Zuma, suspeita de ter ajudado a recrutar 17 sul-africanos sob a promessa de formação em segurança. A ex-parlamentar negou qualquer irregularidade e demitiu-se do Parlamento em Novembro de 2025.
Outro caso envolve a apresentadora de rádio Nonkululeko Mantula, acusada, no final de 2025, de alegadamente recrutar quatro sul-africanos para integrarem o exército russo.
A preocupação com o recrutamento de africanos estende-se a outros países do continente. No Zimbabué, as autoridades anunciaram, em Março, a morte de 15 cidadãos na guerra da Ucrânia e procuravam o regresso de outros 66. Já o Governo do Quénia revelou, em Fevereiro, que mais de mil cidadãos tinham sido recrutados para combater pela Rússia.
Em Março, familiares de cidadãos quenianos protestaram em Nairobi, exigindo o regresso dos seus parentes e a responsabilização dos envolvidos no recrutamento.
Entretanto, após uma cimeira Rússia-África realizada em Moscovo, em Outubro, o Gana e o Quénia anunciaram ter obtido compromissos de Moscovo para pôr fim ao recrutamento dos seus cidadãos, tanto através de esquemas irregulares como do alistamento voluntário.
