items.title: Tahoua accueille la célébration de la 5ème édition de la Journée Nationale du Volontariat axée sur la cohésion sociale

original_payload.original_title: Tahoua accueille la célébration de la 5ème édition de la Journée Nationale du Volontariat axée sur la cohésion sociale
original_payload.original_body:
Tahoua, 10 Novembre (ANP) – Le Secrétaire Général Adjoint du Ministère de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité Publique et de l’Administration du Territoire, M. Abdoulkader Garba Moussa a présidé, ce mardi 10 novembre 2026 dans la salle de conférence de la Mairie de Tahoua, la cérémonie de lancement de la célébration de la 5 ème  édition de la Journée Nationale du Volontariat axée sur le thème « les relais communautaires, acteurs-clés de la cohésion sociale ».
À cette occasion, le Secrétaire Général Adjoint du Ministère de l’intérieur a tenu à adresser ses sincères remerciements aux autorités administratives et coutumières, ainsi qu’à l’ensemble des populations de Tahoua pour l’accueil chaleureux réservé à sa délégation.
Parlant du thème de cette édition, M. Abdoulkader Garba Moussa a indiqué que cette référence à la cohésion sociale comme thème de la présente édition des relais communautaires vient, en quelque sorte, faire écho aux appels maintes fois réitérés du Président de la République, Chef de l’Etat, le Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani et du Premier Ministre Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine pour le renforcement de la cohésion sociale, base de l’édification de la Nation.
Au demeurant, l’un des axes du Programme de la Refondation de la République (PRR 2025-2029) est consacré précisément à la problématique de la cohésion sociale, a-t-il fait observer, tout en rappelant que la proclamation de cette journée ne procède pas du hasard, il s’agit d’un choix délibéré inscrit dans les actes du Guide d’orientation et de référence sur le relais communautaire de développement, adopté le 10 novembre 2017 pour donner un cadre de référence à l’action de ces femmes et de ces hommes de bonne volonté.
Selon lui, cette Journée Nationale, célébrée chaque 10 novembre, vise trois objectifs : informer et sensibiliser les autorités et les partenaires sur l’importance de la contribution des relais au développement local ; promouvoir leurs activités pour le bien-être des communautés et confirmer la reconnaissance de l »État pour les efforts que les relais consentent au bénéfice des populations.
Le SGA du Ministère en charge de l’Administration du Territoire a saisi cette occasion pour présenter ces relais communautaires, qui sont des hommes et de femmes cooptés par leurs communautés sur des critères de disponibilité, d’engagement et de confiance et qui servent de façon volontaire, sans attendre de gloire, dans les domaines de la santé, de la nutrition, de l’éducation, de l’hydraulique, de l’environnement, de l’agriculture et de l’élevage. En outre, ils sont au cœur de la prévention et de la prise en charge des principales maladies de l’enfant, toutes choses qui représentent, pour les populations, le reflet de la proximité de l’action publique et le trait d’union entre les politiques publiques et les réalités locales.
Insistant sur le thème de cette année, M. Abdoulkader Garba rappelle, une fois de plus, qu’il n’y a pas de développement durable sans cohésion sociale, car une communauté divisée ne peut ni produire ensemble, ni protéger ses enfants ensemble, ni gérer ensemble ses ressources. D’où le rôle éminemment important du relai communautaire en tant que vecteur de dynamique positive pour la communauté, laquelle, en retour, se reconnaît en lui.
Après Maradi en 2025, où cette journée s’est tenue sous le thème « le Relai Communautaire à l’ère de la refondation », c’est au tour de Tahoua d’accueillir cette année le lancement de la journée des relais communautaires sous le thème de la cohésion sociale. Le fait est que, a expliqué le SGA du Ministère de l’Intérieur, « dans un contexte où notre pays réaffirme sa volonté de bâtir son développement en mettant l’accent d’abord sur ses propres ressources et ses propres valeurs, les relais communautaires incarnent, à notre sens, un levier supplémentaire sur lequel on peut compter ». Il a notamment salué le rôle de l’Agence Nigérienne de Volontariat pour le Développement, qui œuvre avec constance pour promouvoir l’engagement volontaire et pour encadrer l »action des relais. Il a également salué  l’engagement des partenaires techniques et financiers, des ONG et des associations qui font confiance aux relais pour atteindre les populations. Il s’est, en outre, réjoui de constater que parmi les 130 relais présents à Tahoua, les femmes sont majoritaires, ce qui constitue un message fort car la cohésion sociale se construit aussi et surtout avec les femmes.
M. Abdoulkader Garba Moussa a ensuite informé que depuis l’institution de cette Journée, des avancées significatives ont été enregistrées. Il s’agit notamment de l’institutionnalisation de la Journée elle-même, de la remise de prix de participation et de l’harmonisation de la prime de motivation. Ces résultats, a-t-il souligné, traduisent l’engagement de l’État à mieux structurer et à mieux valoriser le volontariat communautaire.
Aussi, a-t-il demandé aux planificateurs de veiller à ce que les actions de relais s’inscrivent dans la durée et s’intègrent dans les plans de développement communaux et aux relais eux-mêmes de veiller à la maitrise des outils nécessaires à l’accomplissement de leur mission, y compris les outils numériques. Aux autorités administratives et coutumières, il a demandé de veiller à faire des relais communautaires des alliés dans les actions de développement et des partenaires dans les instances de gouvernance locale.
Pour sa part, le Gouverneur de la Région de Tahoua, le Colonel-Major Souleymane Amadou Moussa s’est réjoui d’accueillir la célébration de cette 5 ème  édition de la Journée Nationale de Volontariat, avant d’adresser ses remerciements au SGA du Ministère de l’intérieur, représentant le Ministre d’Etat, le Général de Division Mohamed Toumba, pour le choix porté à sa région pour célébrer cette journée.
Le Gouverneur Souleymane a aussi exprimé sa reconnaissance et l’engagement de la région dans le domaine du volontariat et de la mobilisation générale. Pour lui, cette journée est une occasion de valoriser le rôle des relais communautaires, d’échanger sur les bonnes pratiques entre les 8 Régions, de renforcer leurs capacités dans leur action dans la politique publique de développement. « Elle permet à notre région de s’affirmer comme un acteur engagé dans le cadre de la valorisation de Volontariat à l’ère de la refondation », a-t-il dit avant de prendre trois engagements autour du développement local, de la santé, de l’hydraulique, de l’environnement, l’agriculture, l’élevage pour qu’ils travaillent en synergie avec les relais communautaires.
Pour sa part, le Directeur Général de l’Agence Nigérienne pour le Volontariat de Développement (ANVD), M. Albachir Aboubacar, il a rappelé que ce 10 novembre, « nous ne célébrons pas seulement une date du calendrier, nous magnifions une vision, un choix courageux et une valeur cardinale de notre identité commune : le don de soi pour la patrie. C’est la reconnaissance nationale du rôle fondamental des relais communautaires dans le développement local, la résilience sociale et la mobilisation citoyenne », a-t-il indiqué.
Il a également fait savoir que l »Agence Nigérienne de Volontariat pour le Développement s’est donnée une feuille de route claire : coordonner, structurer, valoriser et pérenniser cet élan citoyen dont il mesure chaque jour l’ampleur des sacrifices des relais communautaires, souvent consentis dans des conditions exigeantes. C’est pourquoi, le DG ANVD a réaffirmé son engagement ferme à œuvrer sans relâche, aux côtés des plus hautes autorités de l’État et des partenaires, pour améliorer leurs conditions de déploiement et renforcer leurs compétences.
Notons que la cérémonie a été marquée par la remise des témoignages de satisfaction et des cadeaux aux relais communautaires de développement.
TSA/KPM/ANP-096 Novembre 2026

items.title: Coopération Niger-Algérie : Accélération majeure du projet de la Route Transsaharienne

original_payload.original_title: Coopération Niger-Algérie : Accélération majeure du projet de la Route Transsaharienne
original_payload.original_body:
Le Niger et l’Algérie franchissent une étape décisive pour transformer le paysage économique régional. Ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, le ministre nigérien de l’Équipement et des Infrastructures, le Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, a tenu une séance de travail capitale avec le secrétaire général du Comité de Liaison de la Route Transsaharienne (CLRT) et l’ambassadeur d’Algérie au Niger. En effet, cette concertation de haut niveau scelle l’engagement des deux nations à concrétiser la Route transsaharienne en un véritable levier de croissance.
L’émergence d’un corridor stratégique
Les discussions se sont principalement concentrées sur l’évaluation rigoureuse du chantier et sur la transition de cet axe routier majeur vers un corridor économique intégré. À cet effet, les diplomates et responsables techniques entendent moderniser la circulation commerciale afin de fluidifier le transit des marchandises du nord au sud du continent. Par ailleurs, la délégation du CLRT effectue une mission d’évaluation sur le terrain nigérien du 9 au 14 novembre 2026, garantissant un contrôle précis des avancées techniques avant la prochaine session d’orientation de l’organisme.

La sélection s’annonce particulièrement exigeante à l’École nationale d’administration (ENA) de Niamey. Depuis ce mardi 10 novembre, 413 candidats participent au concours professionnel des Douanes de niveau I, organisé pour pourvoir seulement cinq postes. items.title: Tchad: un salon national pour dynamiser l’élevage, secteur crucial pour l’économie du pays

original_payload.original_title: Tchad: un salon national pour dynamiser l’élevage, secteur crucial pour l’économie du pays
original_payload.original_body:
Reportage
Tchad: un salon national pour dynamiser l’élevage, secteur crucial pour l’économie du pays
Au Tchad, des éleveurs venus des 23 provinces du pays, des artisans et des transformateurs de produits laitiers, mais surtout les bêtes – vaches, taureaux, zébus, dromadaires, chèvres, béliers ou encore chevaux –, tous sont réunis du 4 au 10 novembre sur la place de la Nation à l’occasion du Salon national de l’élevage du Tchad. Trois concours : poids, laitier et beauté pour sacrer les spécimens les plus remarquables, mais surtout un espace de rencontre et de partage pour les professionnels d’un secteur pastoral crucial.
Publié le :  10/11/2026 - 17:07
2 min     Temps de lecture
Écouter - 01:22
Des bovins exposés au Salon national de l'élevage 2026.        © Nadia Ben Mahfoudh/RFI
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Avec notre correspondante à Ndjamena,   Nadia Ben Mahfoudh
Le président du comité d’organisation du salon fait la visite et présente les bêtes.
Le docteur Abakar Mahamat Nour Malay montre : «  Vous avez uniquement la race kouri, ici. La race kouri, ils n'ont pas de bosse et ils ont un dos rectiligne. Sa robe est généralement complètement blanche avec des grosses cornes bulbeuses.  »
«  Que la production soit progressivement améliorée  »
Le but de ce salon : valoriser le secteur pastoral et son potentiel. «  C'est une manière de montrer les différentes races existantes au   Tchad  , donc un partage d'informations et de bonnes pratiques de l'élevage pour que les autres aussi suivent, afin que la production soit progressivement améliorée  », poursuit le docteur Abakar Mahamat Nour Malay.
Les stars du salon sont les animaux, mais toute une partie est consacrée aux produits animaliers transformés : miel, lait, yaourt ou encore fromage.
Un système pastoral qui fait vivre directement 40 % de la population
Achtar, à la tête de la Ferme Ayoumbou à Amdourman, explique : «  On élève les vaches, les ovins, les bovins, les caprins. On transforme le lait de vache en fromage avec différentes saveurs. Du coup, on valorise un peu les produits locaux. Tout le monde nous dit :   " Vous êtes où ? Vous êtes où ? " Parfois, on manque même de fromage. On est victime de notre succès mais c’est bénéfique.  »
Le système pastoral fait vivre directement 40 % de la population tchadienne.

items.title: RDC: la fermeture de l’aéroport de Bunia prolongé jusqu’au 8 février 2027

original_payload.original_title: RDC: la fermeture de l’aéroport de Bunia prolongé jusqu’au 8 février 2027
original_payload.original_body:
RDC: la fermeture de l’aéroport de Bunia prolongé jusqu’au 8 février 2027
C’est l’une des conséquences de l’épidémie d’Ebola qui frappe l’est de la République démocratique du Congo : l’aéroport international de Bunia ne va pas rouvrir dans les prochaines semaines. Il va rester fermé au moins jusqu’au 8 février 2027, selon une note de la Régie des voies aériennes. Depuis le 23 mai dernier, plus aucun vol commercial n’a été programmé de ou vers la capitale provinciale de l’Ituri.
Publié le :  10/11/2026 - 19:14
1 min     Temps de lecture
Une vue de l'aéroport national de Bunia, au nord-est de la RDC.        © Paulina Zidi/RFI
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Avec notre correspondante à Kinshasa ,  Paulina Zidi
Le nouveau terminal international ne va donc pas encore accueillir ces premiers passagers, tout comme la piste allongée ne va pas voir ces prochains mois les gros porteurs des compagnies commerciales.
Le 23 mai dernier, l’annonce de la fermeture de l’aéroport avait été assez soudaine, laissant des passagers bloqués à Bunia et des vols cargos en souffrance. Une fermeture qui avait été décidée après des pressions diplomatiques, selon des sources sécuritaire, diplomatique et humanitaire.
Même si une réouverture avait été annoncée le 1ᵉʳ juin, elle n’a jamais été actée sur le terrain et seuls les vols humanitaires, sanitaires ou d’urgence restent autorisés.
Plusieurs organisations de la société civile ont dénoncé cette nouvelle décision, mettant en avant l’isolement de la province. D’autant plus que l’état des routes se dégrade pendant la saison des pluies qui est en cours et que certains des axes majeurs de circulation connaissent une situation sécuritaire compliquée avec la présence de groupes armés.
À lire aussi  Ebola en RDC: la suspension des vols à l'aéroport de Bunia met à mal le secteur aérien local

items.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?

original_payload.original_title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
original_payload.original_body:
History    Germany
Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
Helen Whittle
11/10/2026  November 10, 2026    Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.
https://p.dw.com/p/5PGDc
Prefer DW on Google
European colonialism was marked by the — often extremely violent — exploitation of people and resources. [Pictured: Clearing of land by setting grass on fire during a German research expedition to Tendaguru in German East Africa, 1909–1913] Image: Archiv/Museum für Naturkunde       Advertisement
Racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious. In 1941, Nazi dictator  Adolf Hitler  himself compared Eastern Europe to "Germany's India" after the British colonial model, declaring that "like the English, we shall rule this empire with a handful of men."
But the extent to which  Nazism  was shaped by the age of empire, and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared, remains the subject of intense debate. This is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the  Holocaust . Others have argued that the intense focus on the Nazi era has, at least in part, come at the expense of a meaningful reckoning with Germany's colonial history.
'Murder for the very purpose of murder': The industrialized mass murder carried out in Nazi death camps such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka and Auschwitz-Birkenau had no direct precedent in colonial history. [Pictured: Cans of Zyklon B gas, Auschwitz-Birkenau, German Nazi concentration and extermination camp in Poland] Image: Taiftin/Depositphotos/IMAGO
"I do think this is nonsense," says Stephan Malinowski, a Professor of Modern European History at the University of Edinburgh. "If it were true, then all other colonial countries who are not discussing the Holocaust, like Great Britain for example, or France or Spain or Portugal, they would then supposed to be very, very attentive to colonial crimes and to colonial history, which it seems to me is not the case."
"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence," a new exhibition at the German Historical Museum in Berlin curated by Malinowski, does not aim to settle the debate but to tell its story.
From colonial brutality to Nazi rule
The exhibition begins with a hippopotamus-hide whip used in African colonies displayed alongside a canister of Zyklon B, the poison used in Nazi gas chambers. The juxtaposition highlights the contrast between colonial violence and the  industrialized mass murder of the Holocaust . Yet it also points to connections: Whips were used in Nazi concentration camps, while Fascist Italy deployed chemical weapons against civilians and soldiers during its invasion of Ethiopia (then Abyssinia) in 1935-36.
The extreme brutality of Fascist Italy's invasion of Ethiopia, including the use of chemical weapons, caused uproar around the world. [Pictured: The bombing of the Ethiopian village of Dessye by Italian planes] Image: Topfoto/United Archives International/IMAGO
In the 1930s, anti-colonial thinkers from India to the Caribbean argued that colonialism and fascism were two sides of the same coin. "There is nothing new or original about the blustering exploits of Hitler and Mussolini," observed the  Trinidadian  journalist and Pan-Africanist George Padmore in 1938. "They have all been used before by the British in their efforts to obtain the subjection of less powerfully armed and more industrially backward people."
European colonial rule was marked by the ruthless exploitation of people and resources, often enforced through extreme violence. In "The Origins of Totalitarianism" (1951), German-American philosopher  Hannah Arendt  argued that colonial territories served as laboratories for racial ideologies and practices of domination that could be applied beyond the legal constraints of Europe. Arendt described how these later "boomeranged" back into Europe and helped shape totalitarian politics in distinct and unprecedented form.
One of the most notorious symbols of King Leopold II's rule was the amputation of hands, inflicted on men, women and children who failed to meet rubber production quotas. [Pictured: A Congolese child with an amputated hand, circa 1900] Image: United Archives/World History Archive/IMAGO
The Congo Free State,  King Leopold II of Belgium 's private colony from 1885 to 1908, became notorious for its extreme brutality, as colonial authorities used executions, amputations and sexual violence to ensure rubber production quotas were met.  Forced labor was central to Nazi rule , with millions of Poles, Ukrainians, Russians and others from the  Soviet Union , and Jews, subjected to exploitation and "Vernichtung durch Arbeit" ("extermination through work"). Within a few years, the regime mobilized around 13 to 14 million forced laborers, a scale comparable to the  transatlantic slave trade  over more than three centuries. The Nazis sought to extract value from their victims at every stage, confiscating their property, exploiting their labor, and even harvesting gold teeth and hair from the dead.
Racism, antisemitism and extermination
While racism underpinned both colonial empires and Nazism, Malinowski says the goals were different. The colonial powers tended to present assimilation as a path to advancement, forcing colonized people to adopt European culture, serve imperial interests, and suggesting that a select, educated few could gain opportunities at elite institutions such as Oxford or Cambridge. "This is definitely not something that the Nazi regime is offering to Poles or to Russians or let alone to Jews," added Malinowski.
"In terms of violence, colonial violence was just as extreme as Nazi violence. But Nazi violence was annihilatory and exterminatory compared to colonial violence in the colonies," says Edward Kissi, a historian at the School of Interdisciplinary Global Studies at the University of South Florida. He points to the example of how, unlike European colonial powers in Africa, the Nazis pursued the  elimination of Black-Germans or peoples of African descent in Germany through forced sterilization . "Even in racism, colonial color-based racism and colonial anti-Jewish sentiments were fundamentally different from what the Nazis pursued."
From 1904 to 1908, German colonial rule in present-day Namibia culminated in the genocide of the Herero and Nama, in which tens of thousands died. [Pictured: Concentration camp for Herero and Nama in German South West Africa in 1905] Image: Sam-Cohen-Bibliothek/Scientific Society Swakopmund
On October 2, 1904, German General Lothar von Trotha issued the "Vernichtungsbefehl" ("extermination order") following the Herero uprising in German South West Africa (present-day  Namibia ). Historians generally attribute the order to a combination of racial ideology, a desire to terrorize the population into submission, and efforts to secure colonial control over land, labor and resources. Between 1904 and 1908, an estimated  60,000 to 80,000 Herero (around 80% of the population) and 10,000 (around half the population) Nama died.
One area where the exhibition draws no direct parallel is the  industrialized killing carried out in Nazi death camps  such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, and  Auschwitz-Birkenau . "Where the two things really diverge is the Holocaust and is the systematic mass murder of the European Jews and it's murder for the very purpose of murder," explains Malinowski. The deportation of around 1,800 Jews from the Greek islands of Rhodes and Kos in July 1944 illustrates how Nazi persecution often defied military or economic logic. Even after the war was effectively lost, the community was transported to Auschwitz, where most were murdered immediately upon arrival.
The politics of historical comparison
The issue of the "singularity" of the Holocaust came to the fore during the 1980s "Historikerstreit" ("historians' dispute"). Historian  Ernst Nolte  argued that Nazism should be understood in the wider context of 20th-century political violence, and as a response to Bolshevik terror in particular. Critics accused him of downplaying German responsibility for Nazi crimes.
Since 2020, a renewed debate dubbed the "Historikerstreit 2.0" has focused on whether the Holocaust should be viewed as a unique reference point in German memory culture or be understood alongside the histories of colonialism, racism and empire. The dispute now is less about the legitimacy of comparison than about its implications.
After being deported to Auschwitz-Birkenau in 1943, French artist David Olère depicted scenes he witnessed. Here, deportees arrive at a crematorium shortly before their murder. [Pictured: David Olère, 'Vers la mort' ('On the Way to Death'), Paris, 1945] Image: Mémorial de la Shoah/Coll. David Olère
The mass murder of tens of thousands of the Herero and Nama during four years of German colonial rule is now regarded as the first genocide of the 20th-century. In 2016, Nama representatives walked out of talks after Germany's chief negotiator said what happened was "incomparable" to the Holocaust. The German government has  since recognized the events as genocide  "from today's perspective," but it has not yet accepted legal liability or agreed to pay formal reparations.
Rethinking Germany's culture of remembrance
Martinican intellectual Aimé Césaire argued in "Discourse on Colonialism" (1950) that Europe condemned under Nazism forms of violence it had long accepted in its colonies. The exhibition opens amid renewed debates over settler colonialism, the definition of genocide, and the meaning of "never again," sharpened by  Nicaragua's case against Germany at the International Court of Justice  over German support for Israel during the war in Gaza. These tensions are reflected in visitors' comments in the exhibition's epilogue, even though the exhibition itself does not address  Israel or Palestine  beyond a reference to Mohammed Amin al-Husseini, appointed Grand Mufti of Jerusalem in 1921.
Germany has unequivocally accepted responsibility for the Holocaust, which is front and center of the country's culture of remembrance.  However, Kissi likens Germany's apparent reluctance to reckon with its colonial history to debates in the  US over slavery , in  Cambodia over the Khmer Rouge , and in Turkey over the  Armenian genocide . According to him, Germany's contemporary identity cannot be fully understood without examining its colonial history and the ways the Nazis appropriated and transformed aspects of that legacy. "I think Germans and all other human beings who have experienced violent pasts and difficult pasts should be very careful not to delink or dissociate those facts from their present," Kissi said. "These are historical patterns. It is better to deal with these historical patterns and discomforts than to just fight them and then say this has absolutely nothing to do with German national identity."
"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence" is on show at the German Historical Museum until April 11, 2027.
Helen Whittle   British journalist in Berlin
Edited by:  Sarah Judith Hofmann

original_payload.original_title: Ondo APC targets one million votes for Tinubu in 2027
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Ondo APC targets one million votes for Tinubu in 2027
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   2 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Segun Giwa
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ondo State says it is targeting one million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.
The party’s Director-General, Ondo State Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Mr Victor Olabimtan, disclosed this on Tuesday in Akure at a news conference held at the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Ondo State Council.
Olabimtan said the party was determined to surpass its 2023 electoral performance, when Tinubu secured 369,924 votes, representing about 67.1 per cent of the valid votes cast in the state.
He attributed the party’s confidence to the achievements of the Tinubu administration and its development projects across the state.
He listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Ore-Ondo-Akure Road and Ilesha-Akure-Owo-Benin Road among federal infrastructure projects expected to benefit the state.
Olabimtan also cited renewed attention to the proposed Olokola Deep Seaport, the establishment of the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) Teaching Hospital and the proposed Aviation College.
He identified federal student financing initiatives as other interventions by the administration, adding that the appointment of three ministers from Ondo had strengthened the state’s representation at the national level.
The PCC director-general commended Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa for promoting party unity and coordinating grassroots mobilisation across the state’s 18 local government areas.
He said Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, ministers and other national party leaders were expected to attend the party’s presidential campaign rally scheduled for Wednesday in Akure.
According to him, the rally will mark the beginning of sustained mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Olabimtan assured supporters that adequate preparations had been made for the rally.
He urged party leaders and supporters to sustain unity, intensify grassroots engagement and maintain peaceful conduct as they pursue the party’s electoral target.
“This is an achievement we are proud of, but we are not resting on our oars. We are determined to surpass the 2023 record in the 2027 general elections.
“We must strengthen our ward and local government structures, sustain engagement with the electorate and communicate the policies, programmes and achievements of the Tinubu administration in a clear, factual and convincing manner.
“Achieving this ambition will require more than political enthusiasm, identifying unity of purpose, effective coordination, discipline, strategic communication and the active participation of every party member as critical to victory.
“Party leaders, stakeholders and members should place collective interests above personal ambitions and aspirations,” he said. (NAN)
Edited by Ayodeji Alabi

items.title: Nigeria cannot build healthy country on foreign aid – Pate

original_payload.original_title: Nigeria cannot build healthy country on foreign aid – Pate
original_payload.original_body:
Health  Nigeria cannot build healthy country on foreign aid – Pate
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   2 hours ago   ·  6 min read
✓
✓
By Folasade Akpan
The Federal Government has urged Nigerians and state governments to strengthen domestic health financing, saying sustainable healthcare delivery cannot depend on foreign taxpayers.
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Pate, made the call at the opening of the 2026 Joint Annual Review (JAR) in Abuja on Tuesday.
Pate said increased domestic resource mobilisation was essential to sustaining gains from ongoing health sector reforms and reducing dependence on external assistance.
“The illusion that you can have a healthy country on somebody else’s taxpayer, I think we should put it behind us.
“The only way forward is to mobilise, produce, execute domestic financing, and that is still work ahead for us,” he said.
He said the Federal Government was working to increase domestic health financing, adding that the memorandum of understanding with the United States government committed Nigeria to strengthening local funding.
According to him, the commitment is aimed at reducing the country’s dependence on external assistance by 2030.
Pate said legislative measures, including increasing the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) allocation to two per cent and reforms to sugar-sweetened beverage excise taxes, would expand available resources.
He said the reforms, initiated under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, were designed to address longstanding challenges of inadequate financing, fragmented governance and poor coordination.
Others included the unequal distribution of health workers and weaknesses in healthcare delivery, he said.
Pate said the government had adopted a national health systems approach, working with state and local governments, development partners and other stakeholders to align resources and priorities.
He said the approach was anchored on four pillars: strengthening governance, improving population health outcomes, unlocking healthcare value chains, and strengthening health security and resilience.
On financing, Pate said N249 billion had been disbursed to states through the four BHCPF gateways between 2023 and the third quarter of 2026.
He compared this with N74 billion cumulatively disbursed to primary healthcare facilities through direct facility financing in the 10 years preceding the administration.
On healthcare manufacturing, he said 10 factories or production lines had been commissioned, while pharmaceutical manufacturers received N24 billion in tax waivers between 2025 and 2026.
He added that 12 technology transfer agreements had been secured, with prospective investments valued at more than five billion dollars.
“Medipool is in place, which is the group purchasing organisation for the first time, not only here in Nigeria, but on the continent, that you have a major group purchasing organisation to mobilise and organise demand for what the federal government will buy,” he said.
On health security, Pate cited Nigeria’s response to the imported Ebola case as an example of the importance of preparedness and coordinated action.
He said the response by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), its incident management system and partners helped contain the case and prevent further transmission.
The minister, however, identified inadequate and unevenly distributed health workers, quality of care and financing as outstanding challenges requiring attention.
He said the government was working with professional associations to improve incentives for health workers, including remuneration, infrastructure and other working conditions.
Pate also said modernising federal tertiary hospitals, expanding health insurance coverage and accelerating digital transformation, including artificial intelligence applications, would feature in the next phase of reforms.
He commended state governments for their contributions, citing Jigawa’s regular health sector performance reviews and the timely completion of annual operational plans by Abia and Nasarawa.
He also acknowledged Kaduna’s accelerated primary healthcare revitalisation, as well as investments in rural emergency transportation by Kano and Katsina states.
Adamawa was also recognised for efforts to align development partners’ support with state priorities, he said.
“National ownership and international cooperation work together when roles are clear and results reach our people,” he said.
Earlier, Dr Iziaq Salako, Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, said JAR provided an opportunity to assess implementation of the health sector compact and ensure commitments translated into measurable results.
Salako said the review was particularly important as it marked the final phase of the first cycle of the health sector renewal agenda.
This was ahead of 2027, the final year of the 2023–2027 Health Sector Strategic Blueprint, he said.
“JAR is therefore not a mere ceremony, but a working platform to measure performance against the compact, spotlight what works so that others can adopt it.
“It should end with clear resolutions assigned to MDAs, partners and responsible persons, with defined timelines for actions,” he said.
He said the theme of the review, “Together to Higher Ground: Make the Data Count”, underscored the need to ensure health data informed decisions and improved service delivery.
“Every number must be dependable enough to stand by, and every number must be used to change a life.
“It commits us that every data that we collect, store or track must be useful and actionable.
“A mother counted at antenatal visit should be counted at delivery, and a child counted at birth should be counted at every vaccination,” he said.
Salako said Nigeria had enrolled almost eight million additional people in health insurance under the administration, including more than three million vulnerable persons.
He added that more than 8,000 primary healthcare facilities had received direct support, while over 3,000 facilities had been improved to Level Two readiness.
He said facility-reported maternal deaths had declined, while neonatal and under-five deaths had also fallen by 22 per cent and 25 per cent, respectively.
Salako said the review would examine reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health, food and drug regulation, emergency transportation and free maternal and newborn services.
“Other areas included health financing,” he said.
He said the review would also feature the inauguration of the Mini-Demographic and Health Survey report, the National Sexual and Reproductive Health Policy, and tax-shifting and tax-sharing guidelines.
Salako said the expected resolutions should identify responsible departments, agencies and partners, with timelines for implementation and integration into the 2027 Annual Operational Plans.
He said the administration’s longer-term targets included achieving at least 90 per cent functional primary healthcare centres by 2031.
The  News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)  reports that the three-day JAR, which ends on Thursday, brings together federal and state governments, development partners, civil society organisations and private sector representatives.
The meeting provides a platform for stakeholders to assess health sector performance and review progress in implementing ongoing reforms.( NAN )
Edited by Abiemwense Moru

items.title: Petroleum minister hails Wike for transforming Abuja’s infrastructure landscape

original_payload.original_title: Petroleum minister hails Wike for transforming Abuja’s infrastructure landscape
original_payload.original_body:
Metro  Petroleum minister hails Wike for transforming Abuja’s infrastructure landscape
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   4 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Philip Yatai
The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Sen. Heineken Lokpobiri, has lauded the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, for transforming the infrastructural landscape of the nation’s capital.
Lokpobiri gave the commendation on Tuesday while accompanying Wike on an inspection tour of several road projects across the FCT.
Speaking to journalists during the inspection, the minister described the pace of ongoing projects as “unprecedented”.
He noted that having lived in Abuja since his election to the Senate in 2007, he has witnessed various stages of the city’s expansion, but the speed and quality of execution under Wike’s leadership remain unmatched.
“I’ve been in Abuja for about 19 years now, having arrived in 2007 when I was elected to the Senate. The level of development we are seeing in Abuja today is unprecedented.
“Even those who may not particularly like the FCT minister must give it to him—he is delivering infrastructure, and everyone, including his critics, is benefiting from it,” he said.
Lokpobiri expressed astonishment at the progress recorded on the Southern Parkway road project, noting its proximity to his residence at the National Assembly Quarters.
“This morning, when I had the privilege of joining him to inspect these projects, I was amazed. I live in the National Assembly Quarters in Apo, just about two kilometers away, yet I was unaware of the scale of work happening here.
“I never believed in my wildest dreams that a road flagged off just five months ago in July could reach this level of completion,” he added.
Lokpobiri attributed Wike’s achievements to the sustained backing of President Bola Tinubu, congratulating both the President and the FCT minister for their dedication to fulfilling the administration’s mandate.
He called on Nigerians to support public officers who demonstrate exceptional performance, emphasising that constructive encouragement is vital for sustained progress.
“When someone is performing, the least we can do as citizens is to encourage them. The minister has fundamentally changed the landscape of Abuja, and things can only get better from here,” Lokpobiri said.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Wike inspected the ongoing construction of Inner Southern Expressway, from  Area 1 roundabout to Games Village bridges; Southern Parkway, linking Oladipo Diya Road with Ring Road II.
He also inspected the ongoing construction of Arterial Road S1 project in Abuja to connect Ring Road II to the FCT Fire Service Station in the Kaura and Gaduwa district corridors. (NAN)

items.title: Wike promises to deliver Abaji university of science, tech

original_payload.original_title: Wike promises to deliver Abaji university of science, tech
original_payload.original_body:
Education  Wike promises to deliver Abaji university of science, tech
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   4 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Philip Yatai
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has pledged to ensure the completion and inauguration of the University of Science and Technology, Abaji, during his tenure as minister.
Wike made the pledge on Tuesday in Abaji, while addressing stakeholders, leaders, women and youth groups during the All Progressives Congress (APC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) stakeholders’ meeting under the Rainbow Coalition.
Responding directly to requests presented by the Chairman of the Abaji Area Council, Mr Abubakar Abdullahi, the minister assured residents that the project, which has faced long delays, would receive immediate administrative and financial backing.
“Let me tell you, you should thank yourself that it is in your tenure that the university will be open.
“I can’t go back having felt that this is a major problem touching your people,” he said.
He directed his Chief of Staff and relevant agencies to immediately assess the financial requirements needed to operationalise the university, promising that the institution would open before the current administration elapsed.
Highlighting his administration’s track record in the council, Wike pointed out previous interventions, including road construction projects and the establishment of a local police station.
He emphasised that governance must focus on delivering tangible results and improving the living conditions of the populace.
Beyond local infrastructure, the minister rallied the coalition to ensure a complete victory for President Bola Tinubu across all electoral wards and units in Abaji.
He also reassured residents that ongoing power and infrastructure issues in Abaji would be addressed decisively before the elections.
“Governance is about the happiness of the people. When hair dressers, barbers, and artisans are packing out of Abaji to Gwagwalada because of power and facilities, it hurts the local economy. That suffering ends today,” Wike assured.
Earlier, Abdullahi appealed for the urgent completion of the long-overdue university, noting that the institution’s takeoff would naturally drive socio-economic expansion across the territory.
He also highlighted a lingering one-year power outage caused by bottlenecks along the 32-kilometre Kwali-Abaji feeder line, with only two kilometres under Abaji’s jurisdiction.
He pleaded with the FCT minister to use his executive influence to intervene with relevant federal power authorities.
“We know some of these issues are outside your direct jurisdiction, but with your capacity and voice, we know you can come to our rescue,” Abdullahi said.
The chairman commended Wike for the unprecedented developmental strides in the area, which he said were already atracting developments.
He specifically listed major projects delivered to the council, including the construction of a five-kilometer road network that has unlocked major housing developments at the council headquarters.
He equally pointed at the construction of a modern and fully equipped police station and staff accommodation in the area.
“Your Excellency, the people of Abaji will continue to appreciate you for these milestones. This is the first of its kind in our history,” he said.
The traditional leader of the area, the Ona of Abaji, Alhaji Adamu Yunusa, equally said that his people would benefit immensely if the university and the electricity supply issues were addressed. (NAN)

items.title: 2027: Duke seeks opposition unity as PRP unveils manifesto

original_payload.original_title: 2027: Duke seeks opposition unity as PRP unveils manifesto
original_payload.original_body:
Politics  2027: Duke seeks opposition unity as PRP unveils manifesto
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   5 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Grant Onyeke
Presidential candidate of People’s Redemption Party (PRP), Mr Donald Duke, on Tuesday in Abuja unveiled his ‘A Compact for Nigeria’s Renewal’ manifesto.
Duke, at the occasion, urged opposition parties to bridge their differences, not for personal ambition, but to safeguard the nation’s democratic foundations.
He warned that repeating what he called the miscalculations of the 2023 elections in 2027 would bring ‘lasting shame’.
“We erred in 2023 and we are repeating same in 2027. It is said, fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me. The shame will certainly be on us,” he remarked.
Duke called for an unconventional tactical thinking among opposition forces to counter what he termed an ‘unguarded political establishment’.
“David did not defeat Goliath in a wrestling bout, but by strategy and unconventional means,” he stated.
While building on the party’s strategic outlook, PRP National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, said the occasion served as a vital vehicle to transition the party from mere aspirations to governing reality.
Baba-Ahmed praised the party’s presidential candidate and his running mate, Malam Sule Mohammed, alongside more than 500 others candidates.
He described them as models of integrity, competence and courage designed to lead the nation out of its current economic and security quagmire.
The national chairman acknowledged the immense challenges that plagued the party, including competing against incumbent politicians who relied on state power and immense financial resources.
“We will find resistance from politicians who bribe our people for our future, while we ask for trust and the courage to choose quality and integrity,” he said.
He also urged supporters to reject vote-buying, declaring: “Nigeria and Nigerians are not for sale.
Baba-Ahmed outlined the party’s commitment to historic reforms, including what he termed a groundbreaking initiative that required all candidates to sign a binding compact with their constituents.
“This agreement commits aspirants to unprecedented accountability, service and adherence to the foundational values of the 70-year-old progressive movement,” he said.
While emphasising the party’s active role in the emerging Coalition for Democracy, Baba-Ahmed urged candidates to reject ‘politics as usual’ and campaign with sincerity, respect and an unwavering dedication to national redemption.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Duke, in an interview with newsmen shortly after the programme, also spoke on the state of the judiciary and the viability of an opposition coalition.
According to him, a judge’s ruling is a reflection of their personal integrity and a test for the survival of democracy.
“If you go to a match and you have a biased referee, then the integrity of the entire game is compromised,” the former Cross River governor stated.
He, however, expressed hope that the newly-appointed jurists would act without fear or favour, reminding them that their decisions would shape the nation’s future.
Duke also clarified that forming an alliance involved far more than simply selecting a presidential candidate.
He stressed that the coalition must first establish a shared vision for the direction of the country to avoid repeating cycles of poor governance.
While emphasising his commitment to democratic principles within any alliance, Duke noted, “You can’t call for a democrat and you’re not submitting to the rules and to the regulations of democracy.”
He added that if the group reached a consensus on the best candidate to lead, he would gladly support them.
“At the end of the day, I’m a sportsman about it,” the former governor said.
Duke decried what he called severe systemic obstacles placed on the path of opposition parties trying to campaign, citing exorbitant advertising hurdles and sometime, restricted access to public venues.(NAN)

items.title: Union seeks faster disbursement of BOI loans to artisans

original_payload.original_title: Union seeks faster disbursement of BOI loans to artisans
original_payload.original_body:
Metro  Union seeks faster disbursement of BOI loans to artisans
By  Funmilayo Adeyemi   ·   5 hours ago   ·  4 min read
✓
✓
By Funmilayo Adeyemi
The Amalgamated Union of Motor Mechanics and Technicians of Nigeria (AUOMMATON) has appealed to President Bola Tinubu to direct the Bank of Industry (BOI) to expedite the release of loans to support artisans nationwide.
The National President of the union, Dr Oseni Suleiman, made the appeal at its 2026 National Symposium on the War Against Fake Automobile Spare Parts and Adulterated Lubricants on Tuesday in Abuja.
Suleiman said the loans would improve the working conditions, technical capacity and economic well-being of mechanics and other artisans.
He said the union had earlier written to the President on the matter but was renewing its appeal through the symposium.
“We specially appeal to President Bola Tinubu to please direct the Bank of Industry to hasten the release of the loan we applied for, to ameliorate the suffering of Nigerian artisans.
“Letters concerning this matter had been addressed to His Excellency before now. We are equally reminding him now,” he said.
The union president also appealed to the Federal Government to provide three Hilux vans, a Hummer bus and a permanent office complex in Abuja to strengthen its operations.
He said the proposed Nigerian Artisan House would provide a centre for artisans to exchange ideas and develop strategies for improving their skills.
Suleiman also sought the deployment of armed police personnel to support the union’s campaign against counterfeit automobile spare parts and adulterated lubricants.
He said counterfeit products damaged vehicle engines, caused accidents, harmed the environment and undermined the efforts of genuine technicians.
He said the union, with about 14 million members nationwide, was committed to promoting professionalism, technical training and ethical practices in the automotive sector.
Suleiman disclosed that the union had embarked on capacity-building programmes, documentation and identification of members, as well as collaborations with regulatory agencies to improve accountability and enforcement.
He said the union had partnered with NOGALSS National Apex Cooperative Society Ltd. to establish the National Automotive Empowerment Drive.
According to him, the initiative is designed to provide members with access to financing, automotive tools and equipment, workshop modernisation, technical advancement and business development opportunities.
Earlier, the Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammadu Dingyadi, urged the union to comply with its constitution and statutory obligations to ensure stability and effective administration.
Dingyadi, represented by the Registrar of Trade Unions, Rabiu Suhaibu, also advised the union to promote unity and peaceful resolution of internal disputes.
He urged its leadership to ensure inclusive administration and adherence to the union’s constitution, saying these were essential for stability and progress.
The minister commended the union for promoting industrial peace and harmony, describing these as important to membership expansion, financial stability and investment opportunities.
Also speaking, the President of NOGALSS, Comrade Noah Emmanuel, said the partnership with AUOMMATON would connect mechanics, technicians, workshop operators, spare parts dealers and lubricant distributors to financing and other economic opportunities.
He said the partnership would operate through NOGALSS’s digital national economic ecosystem, which connects associations, cooperative businesses and individuals to capital, productive assets, investors, markets and technology.
Emmanuel said the initiative would provide eligible union members with business expansion financing ranging from N1 million to N10 million.
He explained that the facility was not intended for start-ups but for established businesses with at least two years of operations, verifiable business activities, demonstrable turnover and credible records.
He appealed to the union to present 1,000 members for the first phase of the initiative.
The Chairman of the Occasion, Aminu Jalal, described counterfeit spare parts and substandard lubricants as threats to road safety, vehicle owners and the national economy.
Jalal, a former official of the National Automotive Council, said counterfeit products could fail prematurely, increase vehicle maintenance costs and cause accidents.
He urged AUOMMATON to collaborate with the council to organise training programmes to equip mechanics with skills to identify fake and substandard automotive products.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the symposium, themed “Enough is Enough”, brought together technicians, policymakers, regulators and other stakeholders to discuss measures to tackle counterfeit automotive products. (NAN)

items.title: South Africa says South Sudan election preparations inadequate

original_payload.original_title: South Africa says South Sudan election preparations inadequate
original_payload.original_body:
South Sudan is inadequately prepared for elections scheduled for December 22, South Africa told the UN Security Council on Tuesday, citing an African Union assessment that identified shortages of resources and technical expertise.
Addressing the Council in New York, South Africa’s Permanent Representative, Mxolisi Sizo Nkosi, said significant gaps remained in the preparations, raising concerns about the country’s readiness to conduct the polls.
He also expressed concern over worsening humanitarian conditions, restricted aid access and increasing pressure from refugees fleeing neighbouring Sudan.
While reaffirming South Sudan’s sovereign right to determine its electoral process, Nkosi stressed the need to meet legal, financial and operational requirements and ensure broader participation by political parties, women and young people.
South Africa has offered technical assistance and electoral equipment, he said, adding that South Sudanese electoral officials had been invited to observe South Africa’s November 4 local government elections.
South Sudan defended its decision to proceed with the polls, saying the country cannot remain indefinitely under transitional arrangements.
“Elections are not an obstacle to peace,” Deputy Permanent Representative Sabino Edward Nyawella Amaikwey told the Council, describing them as essential to consolidating stability and allowing citizens to choose their leaders.
He criticised what he called disproportionate attention to political actors accused of obstructing implementation of the 2018 peace agreement, warning against further delays to the electoral process.
Rejecting what he described as unverified allegations and politically charged reporting, Nyawella urged the UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) and human rights mechanisms to strengthen consultations with national authorities.
He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to facilitating UNMISS operations, saying obstruction of the mission “has never been, and is not, a policy” of South Sudan.
Denmark warned that holding elections without political consensus, adequate preparations and meaningful participation could deepen divisions and trigger renewed violence.
Ambassador Christina Markus Lassen of Denmark
Ambassador Christina Markus Lassen urged President Salva Kiir and all parties to recommit to the Revitalized Peace Agreement, uphold the ceasefire and pursue inclusive dialogue.
She condemned continued fighting and attacks on humanitarian workers, saying at least 39 aid workers had been killed this year. She also raised concern over displacement and worsening food insecurity.
Lassen reaffirmed Denmark’s support for UNMISS, condemned restrictions on its operations and called for accountability for attacks on peacekeepers.
South Sudan’s leaders must choose “peace over political self-interest”, she said.
Russia cautioned against premature judgments about the country’s readiness for the December elections, urging Security Council members to respect Juba’s authority over the electoral process.
Anna M. Evstigneeva, Russia’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, backed African Union mediation efforts and UNMISS, stressing the importance of a strong central government and unified national armed forces.
She also called for easing or lifting the arms embargo, arguing that it remained a major obstacle to strengthening South Sudan’s security institutions.

items.title: Fatal yellow fever case confirmed in Morobo County

original_payload.original_title: Fatal yellow fever case confirmed in Morobo County
original_payload.original_body:
South Sudan has confirmed a fatal case of yellow fever in Morobo County, Central Equatoria State, involving a 48-year-old farmer who had recently travelled to neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the health ministry said on Tuesday.
The man, a resident of Okaba village in Gulumbi Payam, travelled to Ariwara in the DRC about two weeks before developing symptoms, according to a November 10 ministry statement seen by Radio Tamazuj.
He developed fever, headache, fatigue, chest and joint pain on October 24, followed by nosebleeding three days later. He subsequently developed a generalised body rash on October 29 while receiving treatment at an isolation and treatment unit.
Blood samples initially tested negative for Ebola, but further testing using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) confirmed yellow fever virus infection, the ministry said. The patient died on November 1.
The ministry said it had activated an emergency response in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO), the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and other health partners to investigate the case and prevent further transmission.
It further said a multidisciplinary team comprising clinicians, epidemiologists, laboratory scientists, health promotion specialists and entomologists has been deployed to Morobo to conduct active case searches and contact tracing in Okaba village and Gulumbi Payam.
The investigation will also include reviews of health facility records to identify people with similar symptoms in the preceding two to three weeks, collection of blood samples for testing and mosquito sampling to assess possible local transmission.
The ministry said it would assess community knowledge and practices to inform targeted vaccination campaigns and strengthen cross-border surveillance with health authorities in neighbouring areas of the DRC.
Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne viral disease that can cause fever, jaundice and severe bleeding in serious cases.
The ministry urged residents to use mosquito nets, eliminate mosquito breeding sites and seek immediate medical attention if they develop fever, yellowing of the eyes, dark urine or unusual bleeding. Suspected cases can also be reported through the national toll-free hotline, 6666.

original_payload.original_title: PRESS RELEASE: UNMISS urges inclusive dialogue, protection of civilians, and renewed commitment to sustaining peace in South Sudan
original_payload.original_body:
Home

PRESS RELEASE: UNMISS urges inclusive dialogue, protection of civilians, and renewed commitment to sustaining peace in South Sudan
PRESS RELEASE: UNMISS urges inclusive dialogue, protection of civilians, and renewed commitment to sustaining peace in South Sudan
10 November 2026
Juba, 10 November 2026 –  Briefing the United Nations Security Council today, Anita Kiki Gbeho, the Secretary-General’s Special Representative and Head of the UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS), urged the country’s leaders to end the fighting and engage in inclusive dialogue to reduce tensions and preserve the transition.
“With just 42 days until South Sudan's first planned election as a sovereign state, the country is at a critical juncture” stated Ms. Gbeho.
She noted that key concerns about preparedness persist, including security, logistics, and the ability to deliver elections in an extremely compressed timeframe.
Moreover, uncertainties surrounding the post-election peace process require urgent attention. Key benchmarks of the Revitalized Peace Agreement remain outstanding, highlighting the importance of establishing a clear, credible, and mutually agreed pathway for the continued implementation of the Agreement.
Turning to security, SRSG Gbeho noted a decline in confrontations between the principal signatories but warned that communal violence continues to harm civilians.
She also stated that approximately 10 million people need humanitarian assistance, while access restrictions have risen by 38 per cent over the past year. Despite these obstacles, UNMISS has recently doubled its humanitarian protection escorts, helping aid reach more than 321,000 people.
Ms. Gbeho appealed to all parties to stop fighting, uphold the ceasefire, and protect civilians; guarantee humanitarian access and UNMISS freedom of movement; and begin expanded, inclusive political dialogue without delay.
“Ultimately, the challenge facing South Sudan is not simply whether elections can be held on December 22 or not. It is whether the remainder of the transition can preserve peace, strengthen public confidence and deliver on the commitments made to the people of South Sudan,” she concluded.
--

items.title: Remarks by Anita Kiki Gbeho, Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of UNMISS, to the United Nations Security Council [Near Verbatim]

original_payload.original_title: Remarks by Anita Kiki Gbeho, Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of UNMISS, to the United Nations Security Council [Near Verbatim]
original_payload.original_body:
Home
Press releases
Remarks by Anita Kiki Gbeho, Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of UNMISS, to the United Nations Security Council [Near Verbatim]
Remarks by Anita Kiki Gbeho, Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of UNMISS, to the United Nations Security Council [Near Verbatim]
10 November 2026
Madam President,
With just 42 days until South Sudan's planned first elections as a sovereign state, the country is at a critical juncture.
Since my last briefing, elections have dominated the political discourse, while the consensus around the transition has become increasingly fragile.
The central challenge facing South Sudan today is whether the transition remains anchored in the Revitalized Peace Agreement and whether the gains of recent years can be preserved and sustained beyond the elections.
Madam President,
Legislative amendments to the National Elections Act were adopted on September 21. The Transitional Government of National Unity was dissolved on September 22 and replaced by a caretaker administration that same day.
The Government has consistently maintained that these measures are intended to facilitate elections and advance the transition. In my engagements with Government officials, I have found a clear determination to proceed with the elections on the 22nd of December.
While the Inter-Party Dialogue was conducted and its outcome remains pending, some opposition groups remained outside the process. The SPLM/A-IO has maintained that the release of Dr. Riek Machar is a prerequisite for its participation in dialogue.
Key concerns about preparedness persist, including security arrangements, logistics, the National Electoral Commission's ability to deliver elections within an extremely compressed timeframe, and the implementation of outstanding provisions of the Peace Agreement.
The recent political changes also fall short of achieving the Peace Agreement's 35 per cent quota for women's representation.
The Sudan People's Liberation Movement (SPLM) is already conducting its nationwide primaries, while very limited electoral activity has been observed among other registered political parties.
As I noted in my last briefing, elections must be a milestone in the transition, not its conclusion. Elections cannot substitute for political dialogue, confidence-building and continued implementation of the Peace Agreement.
Madam President,
On the security front, the picture has become more complex. The fragile political landscape has not resulted in the large-scale conflict of the kind previously experienced. Our data shows that armed confrontations between the principal signatories have generally declined.
However, year-to-date, the number of people killed, injured and displaced has increased. Local grievances, factional divisions and competition over resources have increased and undermine confidence in the broader security environment.
For example, in Jonglei, confrontations involving government and opposition-aligned local forces, combined with the mobilization of armed youth, continue to threaten civilians and undermine stability.
In Unity State, divisions within the SPLM/A-IO have contributed to clashes around Leer and Rubkona Counties.
Violence in Rumbek and Greater Tonj Counties last month, which reportedly left more than 140 people dead, is a stark reminder of the human cost of local conflicts.
Communal violence remains the principal driver of civilian harm, accounting for more than 60 per cent of reported casualties this year.
Overall, addressing local tensions, strengthening accountability, and ensuring governance mechanisms are capable of deterring violence and resolving disputes are needed at all levels.
Madam President,
UNMISS is doing its utmost to support prevention and response measures in line with Security Council Resolution 2820.
For example, in Rumbek, UNMISS rapidly deployed to help protect civilians, secure the local hospital and assist humanitarian partners.
In Mundri East County, local conflict prevention efforts also contributed to the release of 72 abductees.
UNMISS has further streamlined its structure following an internal review and adapted its posture to align resources more closely with mandate priorities and areas of greater risk.
Force and Police are also implementing recommendations from the Military and Police Capability Study requested by the Council, including rebalancing the troop ratio between support and patrolling elements.
The Mission’s recalibration is yielding results. The Mission has doubled its Force protection tasks in support of humanitarians, enabling life-saving assistance to reach more than 321,000 vulnerable people since my last brief.
Madam President,
These efforts are not without challenges and risks.
In August, during a mission to a conflict area in Jonglei, three peacekeepers were killed, UN and national counterparts were injured. We extend our condolences to their families for the loss of their loved ones who gave their lives in the service of peace.
Our ability to fully deliver on the mandate also depends on being able to move freely, safely and predictably throughout the country. Freedom of movement is a protection issue.
Humanitarian access constraints have increased by 38 per cent over the past year. Delays in acknowledgements, including for Force protection, affected Ebola preparedness activities and humanitarian drought assessments in parts of the Equatorias.
Despite some assurances, UNMISS also continues to face movement restrictions in conflict-affected areas, including along the Sobat River corridor, limiting the Mission's ability to respond to protection concerns and support humanitarian operations.
Madam President,
Unfortunately, the humanitarian situation continues to worsen.
Approximately 10 million people require some form of humanitarian assistance. 1.4 million people have crossed into South Sudan since fighting broke out in Sudan.
An estimated 7.5 million people are food insecure. The number of people at risk of famine has increased. Climate change will further impact the prolonged dry spells and anticipated El Niño-induced flooding.
The regional Ebola outbreak adds another layer of risk and underscores the need for preparedness, cooperation and response.
If left unaddressed, political, security, and humanitarian challenges risk reinforcing one another, further exacerbating tensions and vulnerabilities across the country.
Madam President,
As parts of the greater Horn of Africa continue to confront conflict, displacement, and public health challenges, promoting stability in South Sudan remains a regional and international imperative.
Over this period, I have intensified engagement to help prevent escalation and preserve political space.
This has included engagements with President Salva Kiir and national stakeholders; outreach with neighboring countries; strengthened coordination with former President Kikwete; and regular consultations with the African Union and IGAD and the broader diplomatic community in Juba.
I welcome the continued efforts of the region and the AU High Representative, former President Jakaya Kikwete, including efforts to implement the C5+ recommendations and establish a joint AU-UN-IGAD mechanism to support these engagements.
The region can play an important role in encouraging consensus on the next phase of the transition.
However, the responsibility for charting the way forward rests with South Sudanese leaders. Renewed dialogue is needed now to focus on establishing a clear and credible roadmap for completing the outstanding provisions of the Revitalized Peace Agreement.
This would help build confidence, reduce uncertainty, and address some of the root causes of the conflict beyond the electoral period.
Madam President,
Allow me to conclude with four messages.
First, the fighting must stop. All parties must exercise restraint, protect civilians and uphold the ceasefire.
Second, unhindered humanitarian access and UNMISS freedom of movement saves lives and must be guaranteed in practice, not just in principle.
Third, political dialogue cannot wait. South Sudan's leaders should engage in an expanded and inclusive dialogue on the remaining provisions of the Agreement and the path beyond elections.
Fourth, support the AU C5+ declaration of 29 September, particularly its call for expanded and inclusive political dialogue on the remaining milestones of the Peace Agreement, and the consideration of the release of all political detainees.
Ultimately, the challenge facing South Sudan is not simply whether elections can be held on December 22 or not. It is whether the remainder of the transition can preserve peace, strengthen public confidence and deliver on the commitments made to the people of South Sudan.
The true measure of success is simple: whether South Sudanese citizens are safer tomorrow than they are today.
I thank you.
--

items.title: Tchad : les Chambres foncières officiellement opérationnelles pour renforcer le traitement des litiges fonciers

original_payload.original_title: Tchad : les Chambres foncières officiellement opérationnelles pour renforcer le traitement des litiges fonciers
original_payload.original_body:
Les ministres de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, chargée des Droits humains, Ndolenodji Alixe Naïmbaye, et de l’Aménagement du territoire ont procédé, ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, à l’opérationnalisation des Chambres foncières.
La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence de la Secrétaire d’État auprès du ministère de la Justice, des secrétaires généraux et cadres des deux départements ministériels, ainsi que des magistrats et auxiliaires de justice. Cette initiative marque une nouvelle étape dans l’amélioration du traitement des litiges fonciers, à travers une collaboration entre les institutions judiciaires et les services techniques compétents.
À cette occasion, la Garde des Sceaux a salué une avancée majeure pour le système judiciaire tchadien. Elle a souligné que la mise en place de ces chambres traduit la volonté des pouvoirs publics de mieux répondre aux conflits fonciers, qui affectent les familles, la sécurité des biens et la confiance des citoyens envers l’État.
Elle a rappelé que cette réforme découle de la Loi n°010/AN-SENAT/2025 du 9 décembre 2025, portant réforme du Code de l’organisation judiciaire. Désormais, les Chambres foncières sont compétentes pour connaître des litiges relevant de leur domaine. Conformément à l’article 54 dudit Code, les justices de paix ne sont pas compétentes pour connaître des affaires relatives aux droits réels sur les immeubles immatriculés, aux privilèges et aux hypothèques. Les juridictions concernées sont ainsi invitées à se dessaisir des dossiers relevant de cette compétence et à les transmettre aux chambres compétentes.
La ministre a également insisté sur la nécessité de garantir à chaque citoyen, sans distinction de condition sociale, un accès à une justice équitable, impartiale et indépendante, au service de la paix sociale et de l’État de droit.
Enfin, les différents acteurs du dispositif ont été appelés à exercer leurs missions avec détermination, sans céder aux intimidations, et à dénoncer toute tentative d’ingérence dans le fonctionnement de la justice.

items.title: Tchad – Santé : le CEDIRAA plaide pour la mise en place d’un réseau national de lutte contre les addictions

original_payload.original_title: Tchad – Santé : le CEDIRAA plaide pour la mise en place d’un réseau national de lutte contre les addictions
original_payload.original_body:
Le Centre diocésain de recherche et d’accompagnement des addictions (CEDIRAA) appelle les autorités tchadiennes à mettre en place une véritable stratégie nationale de prévention et de prise en charge des addictions. Cet appel a été lancé ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, à l’occasion d’une conférence de presse organisée au terme d’une formation de six jours ayant réuni 31 professionnels de santé issus de neuf provinces du pays.
Animée par Sœur Aurélie Roiné, directrice du CEDIRAA, et le Dr Marileine Kemme, médecin addictologue venue du Cameroun, cette rencontre avec les médias a permis de faire le bilan de la formation et d’évoquer les perspectives de développement de l’addictologie au Tchad.
Pour Sœur Aurélie Roiné, cette initiative constitue une première étape vers la création d’un réseau national de professionnels spécialisés dans la prise en charge des addictions. Elle a notamment déploré l’insuffisance des structures spécialisées et le manque de ressources humaines qualifiées, alors que de nombreux patients vivant en province n’ont pas accès à des soins adaptés.
La directrice a rappelé que le CEDIRAA reste le seul centre spécialisé du pays, avec environ 60 hospitalisations par an pour des dépendances à l’alcool, au tabac, au cannabis, au tramadol et au « Colorado ». Malgré des moyens limités, le centre affiche un taux de réussite de 75 % en matière d’abstinence.
« Tout malade a droit à des soins de qualité à proximité de chez lui », a-t-elle insisté, appelant l’État à soutenir la mise en place d’une réponse nationale afin de permettre aux personnes souffrant d’addictions d’accéder aux soins sans être contraintes de quitter leur province et leur famille.
La formation a bénéficié à 31 soignants issus du Moyen-Chari, du Logone Oriental, du Logone Occidental, du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest, du Mayo-Kebbi Est, de la Tandjilé, du Guéra, du Ouaddaï et de N’Djamena. Selon les organisatrices, cette initiative constitue le socle d’un futur réseau national d’addictologie.
De son côté, le Dr Marileine Kemme a partagé l’expérience camerounaise en matière de prévention et de prise en charge des addictions. Une expérience présentée comme une source d’inspiration pour le Tchad, sous réserve de son adaptation aux réalités locales.
Les deux intervenantes ont enfin salué l’appui financier et logistique de l’Ambassade de France, ainsi que la contribution des professionnels des médias à la sensibilisation du public sur les enjeux liés aux addictions et à la santé mentale.

items.title: Fne 2026 : le panel 3 met en lumière les opportunités offertes aux jeunes par les partenaires de l’Onape.

original_payload.original_title: Fne 2026 : le panel 3 met en lumière les opportunités offertes aux jeunes par les partenaires de l’Onape.
original_payload.original_body:
Dans le cadre des travaux du Forum National sur l’Emploi (FNE 2026), les réflexions se sont poursuivies avec la tenue du Panel 3, consacré au thème : « Opportunités proposées par les partenaires de l’ONAPE ». Cette session a constitué un cadre d’échanges autour des mécanismes et des initiatives susceptibles de faciliter l’accès des jeunes Tchadiens au marché du travail.
Au cœur des discussions, la question de l’insertion professionnelle des jeunes a occupé une place centrale. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur les opportunités concrètes offertes à travers les partenariats de l’Office National pour la Promotion de l’Emploi (ONAPE), notamment en matière d’emploi, de stages professionnels, de formation par apprentissage et d’accompagnement à l’entrepreneuriat.
Ce panel a permis de mettre en évidence l’importance de la collaboration entre l’ONAPE, ses partenaires techniques et financiers, les entreprises ainsi que les différents acteurs du monde professionnel. Ces partenariats constituent en effet des leviers essentiels pour rapprocher les jeunes des opportunités économiques, développer leurs compétences et faciliter leur accès à des emplois décents et durables.
Les échanges ont également souligné la nécessité de renforcer les dispositifs d’accompagnement, de multiplier les passerelles entre la formation et le monde de l’entreprise et de promouvoir des initiatives innovantes en faveur de l’autonomisation des jeunes.
À travers cette rencontre, le FNE 2026 réaffirme l’importance d’une mobilisation collective pour répondre efficacement aux défis de l’emploi et du chômage des jeunes au Tchad. Il s’agit désormais de faire en sorte que les engagements et les partenariats noués se traduisent par des actions concrètes et des résultats mesurables sur le terrain.
En définitive, ce Panel 3 rappelle que les partenariats ne doivent pas être de simples cadres de concertation, mais de véritables instruments d’insertion professionnelle, d’entrepreneuriat et de création d’emplois.
Ensemble, l’ONAPE et ses partenaires entendent faire des opportunités professionnelles un moteur d’espoir, d’autonomisation et de développement pour la jeunesse tchadienne.
